LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9 Imagn Images In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts , winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year. Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars live Date: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Jaguars have the ball The Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision. The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler. Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington , who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks ( Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins ) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented. Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr . and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.) The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange . Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone. When the Ravens have the ball You can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once. Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football. Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night. The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Now Playing Share Share Video Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? There will not be any Trevor Lawrence-Lamar Jackson round three due to an injury to Jackson. We won't see Tyler Huntley either, with Ravens undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano set to make the start. But there will still be a big stage for the Jaguars, along with a big opportunity. The Jaguars are fighting through their own injuries , losing Davon Hamilton and Eric Murray to season-ending injuries during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Add in running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker being questionable, and the Jaguars are a bit dinged up themselves. But if the Jaguars can overcome the challenge of a road trip against a talented team on a short week, they can do more than prove their mettle. They can be 6-2 entering a stretch where they play the Tennessee Titans twice in a three-week span, giving them a chance to have real-deal playoff-clinching scenarios in December. How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. It feels weird on the Jaguars end of things, but that is because every game has stakes when you are a good team, and the Jaguars are indeed a good team. The Jaguars have a big chance to make some clear headway toward a potential No. 1 seed in the AFC. They are clumped together right now with the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but they have to get by a rookie quarterback tonight before facing Cam Ward twice and J.J. McCarthy. If the Jaguars go on a run, they could be 9-2 by right after Thanksgiving. That would make them far more than just contenders in the AFC, and it would start with beating Baltimore. Things could have gotten much more interesting had Jackson been available, but the Jaguars will instead face the dreaded backup quarterback in primetime. Weirdly enough, two of the six losses in the Liam Coen era have been to backup quarterbacks after the Jaguars lost to Jake Browning and Davis Mills a year ago. The only other quarterbacks to beat the Jaguars in the regular-season in that span: Sam Darnold, Matt Stafford, Bo Nix, and CJ Stroud. The Jaguars have beaten other backup and rookie quarterbacks in that span, defeating Jacoby Brissett, Cam Ward (twice), Brady Cook, Riley Leonard, and for some reason, Philip Rivers last season. This season, they have gotten wins against a few guys who have played in the Super Bowl in Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow, and Drake Maye. Add in wins against Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy and Stroud last year, and the argument thatg the Jaguars have beaten up on bad quarterbacks doesn't make much sense. The Jaguars are a good team, and I expect Anthony Campanile's defense to get after the Ravens' young passer. Campanile likes to blitz and pressure quarterbacks into intentionally throwing the ball quickly, which helps the defense dictate where the ball will go in coverage. When you know where the ball is going, you can make plays on it or tackle and rally and make stops like the Jaguars have done for two years. Seven of Jacksonville's pressures have resulted in turnovers, tied for the most in the league, and the Jaguars have generated 31 unblocked pressures, tied for second-most. This means the Jaguars' pressures are leading to big plays on the back end, and they force the issue with opposing quarterbacks. Against a young quarterback and a running game that has lesser numbers without Lamar Jackson, I think the Jaguars win this game with field position and red-zone stops. Jaguars 30, Ravens 13. The Jacksonville Jaguars are expected to be without defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn quad. With the trade deadline approaching, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN noted that the Jaguars' need for a defensive tackle has been amplified due to the injury. He also reported that the belief in league circles was that the team would explore upgrades on the line before the injury. Jacksonville Jaguars Ramping Up Search for Defensive Line Help John Shipley of Jaguars OnSI noted that the Jaguars needed to improve their pass rush, and that could have been in the form of a defensive lineman prior to the game. “Simply put, if the Jaguars struggle to impact Jones with their pass-rush on Sunday, then they will have to raise the urgency to add a pass-rusher at the deadline,” wrote Shipley on the Jaguars' need prior to Week 8. “Regardless of whether it is edge help or interior defensive line reinforcements, this game and matchup should tell the Jaguars how badly they need to add some help.” The issue now is that Hamilton was their best run-defending threat. They went from needing a pass-rushing interior lineman to a player who can impact the game in both the pass and run. So, they will either need to take a bigger swing or look to take multiple swings on the line. Shipley acknowledged the difference after the game. “Jacksonville was likely already in the market for a pocket-pushing three-technique who could make an impact on passing downs next to Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, Arik Armstead, and Ruke Orhorhoro,” he added. “That is still a need, too. But now so is nose tackle.” Shipley adds that Roy Lopez of the Arizona Cardinals, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and Moro Ojomo of the Philadelphia Eagles are the names to watch for. Jaguars Might Be Without Hamilton After 2026 The big question for Hamilton is whether he will be with the team after this season. Hamilton will be entering free agency after the year. away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. home.blurb: The Jaguars posted their final injury report against the Ravens. Antonio Johnson is good to go, even though he was a limited participant in practice this season. Then again, easing him back into action was probably the best course of action, so he's back at full strength, or as close to it, on Sunday Night Football. While Johnson is good to go, defensive end Travon Walker (rib) and running back Bhaysul Tuten are listed as questionable. Head coach Liam Coen stated that Tuten will be a game-time decision . Offensive guard Ezra Cleveland was limited in practice due to knee and ankle injuries, but Coen says he'll suit up against the Ravens. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), and running back Chris Rodriguez also practiced on a limited basis but were cleared to play. With Johnson back in the fold, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile will be able to get creative in an effort to overwhelm 2026 third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, who'll get the starting nod with Lamar Johnson and Tyler Huntley out for the season. Aside from Johnson, Jacksonville also has Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III at safety. The Jacksonville Jaguars will face off against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night. Although there's a chance running back Bhayshul Tuten won't suit up for the game, the Jags will get reinforcements on defense . Antonio Johnson will be back after missing the win over the Indianapolis Colts due to an ankle injury. home.blurb: Offensive linemen Vega Ioane and Ronnie Stanley, linebacker Roquan Smith, outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, and running back Justice Hill were all upgraded from limited to full participation on Baltimore's latest Week 9 injury report. The improvements provide some much-needed optimism for a Ravens team dealing with significant injuries during a short week. However, quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley remained out of practice, along with safety Jaylinn Hawkins. Defensive lineman Calais Campbell also did not participate, although his absence was designated as rest rather than an injury. *Fagnano's Monday estimated limited participation was separately confirmed. He does not appear on the Tuesday team graphic and was a full participant. Randall remains designated for return from injured reserve. Ioane's return to full participation is particularly significant after the rookie right guard dealt with an MCL sprain that limited his availability. He participated on a limited basis Monday before being upgraded Tuesday, giving Baltimore a potential boost along the interior offensive line. Stanley also returned to full participation after being limited Monday because of a combination of rest, toe and ankle issues. The Ravens still have questions elsewhere along the offensive line. Right tackle Roger Rosengarten remained limited with an ankle injury, while guard John Simpson was limited because of a back injury. Defensive tackle John Jenkins also remained limited with a knee injury. With undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano preparing to make his first NFL start against Jacksonville, Baltimore's offensive linemen will be particularly important. The Ravens allowed four sacks and struggled to produce consistently against Buffalo. Jackson did not practice Tuesday because of the right thumb injury he suffered against Buffalo. The two-time NFL MVP is expected to undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve, sidelining him for at least four games. Huntley also remained out with a turf toe injury. Coach Jesse Minter acknowledged Tuesday that the veteran backup could be an injured reserve candidate, potentially leaving Baltimore without its top two quarterbacks for an extended period. Minter has already named Fagnano the starter for Thursday's matchup. The rookie practiced Tuesday wearing a substantial brace on his right ankle after being listed as limited during Monday's estimated walkthrough. Smith had been limited because of a foot injury, while Hendrickson was managing finger and rib issues. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was a full participant for the second straight day despite being listed with a stinger, while safety Hawkins remained sidelined with a knee injury. Tight ends Mark Andrews and Matthew Hibner also practiced fully despite hand injuries. Running back Adam Randall, who has been designated to return from injured reserve, was a full participant as he continues working back from a neck injury. Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season. Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback. Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining. The Baltimore Ravens are facing growing uncertainty surrounding Lamar Jackson, Jackson's right thumb injury has become a major setback for Baltimore. Rookie Joe Fagnano completed just 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards and threw two interceptions in his first NFL start. The Ravens fell to 4-5 after suffering their fourth consecutive loss.

home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins. The Cincinnati Bengals need extra luggage to carry all their momentum to Madrid, aiming to extend their winning ways versus the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday morning. Cincinnati is laying just over a field goal inside Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, riding a three-game streak into Week 9 but building that run against some softer opposition. My Bengals vs. Falcons predictions size up the edges for this international encounter, giving my best NFL picks to wake up to on Nov. 8, starring Tee Higgins. Bengals vs Falcons prediction: Falcons +3.5 The Cincinnati Bengals are rolling right now, but those victories have come against some weaker opponents. They took down bottom-feeders like Miami and Tennessee (barely), while needing a second-half rally to overcome Baltimore and a backup QB. There was also a bye in Week 6 giving Cincy a breather. I believe the Bengals should be the favorites in Spain, but not by this many points. The Atlanta Falcons are coming off a strange Week 8 loss in which weather played a huge role in the result. That included four interceptions from QB Michael Penix Jr. , who had only one INT in the previous five starts. I'm not discounting Atlanta too much for that rain-soaked squash at Tampa Bay. Rather, I see the Falcons facing one of the easier defenses on their recent schedule, with the Bengals stop unit slipping the past three games. The most notable dip has come defending the run. The Bengals are allowing 5.1 yards per carry in their last three outings (second most in the NFL). Not what you want to see when staring down Bijan Robinson . Bengals vs Falcons combo The Bengals should be favorites, but their current three-game win streak is very puffed up, and Atlanta poses a stiffer test on a neutral field. I'll take Atlanta on the other side of a field goal. Chase Brown hasn't found paydirt since Week 1. The Falcons have given up 11 total touchdowns to running backs and Brown is a dual-threat option, either running it past the goal line or catching a TD strike. Tee Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league. He's the top-rated WR versus man coverage and faces plenty of one-on-one coverage from Atlanta. Projections call for another big day, with most models north of 80 yards receiving from Higgins. Chase Brown touchdown Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards TOP PICK Bengals vs Falcons player prop: Tee Higgins 75+ receiving yards Bengals receiver Tee Higgins is coming off a monster day versus Tennessee, drawing 11 targets for 10 catches and 155 yards. Higgins could be the best WR2 in the league, with Ja'Marr Chase drawing the ire of the secondary and leaving the 6-foot-4 Higgins with softer matchups. He gets a perfect pairing against Atlanta in Madrid. The Falcons rank 24th in DVOA defending WR2s , allowing an average of 54.6 yards per game to the position. This secondary is also running a high rate of man coverage (10th most), and Higgins currently rates as the No. 1 WR versus man at PFF. Projections for Higgins range from 74 to 88 yards on Sunday morning, with most models north of 80 yards. My number comes out to 81.5 receiving yards in Madrid. Want more NFL player props? Cincinnati and Atlanta will do battle in Spain in a game that could deliver plenty of fireworks for fans. The NFL sent two incredible offensive teams to Madrid that could put up plenty of points. After all, exciting games like this one can really expand the league's footprint on the international stage. Both teams have quite a lot in common. They are both in extremely tight division races where just one win could propel them into first place. However, the difference between the AFC North and the NFC South is absolutely massive. Still, the Falcons have looked impressive at times throughout the season. Meanwhile, the Bengals have been fairly consistent now that their defense is finally looking solid. Though they did not look good against the Titans last week. Regardless, both teams are hungry for a win and have all the offensive weapons needed to get it done. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? And will this game become an offensive shootout or a defensive struggle? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this huge international clash between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid. Joe Burrow has a repeat of his Week 8 offensive explosion against the Falcons Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Bengals looked like a vintage version of the team in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Yes, Cincinnati did get the win. But it was shocking how much they needed to lean on Burrow to get the job done. Fortunately, Burrow is one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL and passed that tough test with flying colors. Burrow finished 38-of-48 for 462 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. He also had one rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback simply put the team on his back and willed them to victory. Now Burrow and friends must face an average Falcons defense that's allowed 223.4 passing yards per game this season. Keep in mind that the best opponent Atlanta has faced this season is Chicago. In that game, Caleb Williams shredded their secondary for 305 passing yards. Beyond that game, the Falcons have not been tested very much through the air this season. So just how much damage could Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins do against the Falcons? Burrow will have a repeat performance from last week, going over 400 passing yards and throwing at least three touchdown passes. Cincinnati has to throw the ball to win right now, so they'll be comfortable going guns blazing. To make this even bolder, both Higgins and Chase will each go over 100 receiving yards and score a touchdown. Bijan Robinson will have twice as many rushing yards as the Bengals The disparity between Atlanta and Cincinnati's running game is absolutely massive. Cincinnati has one of the worst rushing attacks in the entire league. In fact, they only average 80.3 rushing yards per game so far this season. That average is quite concerning since they've already played in seven games, so a few bad performances aren't dragging it down. Chase Brown and company just aren't getting the job done. Atlanta is the exact opposite, with their Bijan Robinson-led rushing attack as one of the best in the NFL. They've averaged 134.8 rushing yards per game this year. Only the Buccaneers, Bears, and Bills have a better average. Robinson is the main reason why the Falcons have such a huge advantage on the ground. Just how good will he do in comparison to the Bengals in Madrid? Bijan is averaging 100.6 rushing yards per game in 2026. He is single-handedly outperforming the Bengals on the ground despite failing to break 100 rushing yards in four consecutive games. The Falcons know that they need Robinson to pop off if they want a chance to win this game. They'll design a game plan to do exactly that, and it has a great chance to work. Bijan won't just have more rushing yards than the Bengals, he'll double them up. All it would take is an elite game by Robinson and a pass-happy attack from Cincinnati's offense. Falcons, Bengals combine for at least 80 points in an exciting shootout in Madrid Image Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images This game has all the necessary ingredients of an offensive shootout. Burrow and friends should have no problem scoring at will in this game. Bijan and the Falcons have a huge advantage running the ball. That should keep their offense consistent throughout this game, even if the Bengals start running up the score. Make no mistake, the Bengals have a solid defense that is both frisky and opportunistic. They won't be playing to their strengths when going up against Bijan on the ground. But once the offense gets established, Cincinnati could start to pull away. They should come away with the victory as long as nothing too fluky happens. The Bengals will come out on top thanks to their high-powered offense than can score at the drop of a hat. If they need points late in this game, they will make it happen. The same is not true for the Falcons. Related: NFL picks, predictions, odds for Week 9: Can home dogs bite? Related: NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: D/ST

Still, with the Bengals' defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Cincinnati opened as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta, with the Bengals listed at -225 on the moneyline and the Falcons at +188. The opening over/under was set at 49.5 points. The latest FanDuel odds show Cincinnati remaining a 3.5-point favorite, although the price has shifted to -102 for the Bengals and -120 for the Falcons. The Bengals' moneyline has moved to -184, while Atlanta's stands at +154. The over/under has increased by one point to 50.5. The Bengals enter the matchup following a wild 43-36 overtime victory over Tennessee that featured five touchdown passes and three interceptions from Burrow, who ultimately delivered the winning score by scrambling nine yards around left end for just the second offensive overtime touchdown in franchise history. But while Cincinnati's offense once again demonstrated its ability to put points on the scoreboard, the defense raised serious questions. The Bengals surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered Sunday's game with just one victory, delivering a performance that looked disturbingly similar to the defensive struggles that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Atlanta, meanwhile, is coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that did not complete a single pass. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn't find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. away.blurb: For fantasy managers, the evidence supports treating Chase as available, and the Week 9 slate offers little reason to sit him. The final inactive report remains the last confirmation before kickoff, and no verified report currently suggests a restriction. The bigger problem sits with Atlanta. Higgins is coming off a 155-yard afternoon, and Chase just produced 141 yards of his own. Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns through seven games. If the full group is available Sunday, the Falcons have to defend a passing attack that spreads the ball without moving away from its top receiver. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR's Status Before Falcons Matchup By Nishat | November 4, 2026 | Featured , NFL Ja'Marr Chase enters Week 9 in Madrid off the best receiving afternoon of his season. He caught 11 passes for 141 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans , and he found the end zone in that same game. The only open question was whether the short turnaround to Spain changed anything. Cincinnati's latest injury report answered it. Chase is not listed on the Week 9 injury report. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Gives Bengals WR Clear Status The Bengals left Chase off their Wednesday report entirely. That report was only an estimate because the team held a walkthrough instead of a full practice, but it did not carry any new designation for the club's top receiver. Chase also made the trip. He traveled with the team to Madrid on Tuesday, and Bengals.com published a travel photo identifying him among the players on board ahead of the league's international weekend against the Atlanta Falcons . That leaves no verified reason to describe Chase as injured. The report instead points toward normal availability, though the inactive list will not be final until game day. The Week 8 outing was his strongest of the season. Chase caught 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards against the Titans, with a 30-yard long and one trip to the end zone. His 16 targets were a season high. The performance pushed his 2026 totals to 43 catches for 492 yards, and he has six touchdowns through seven games, according to NFL statistics. Joe Burrow played one of his strongest games of the season as well. He completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards against Tennessee. He threw five passing touchdowns in that game and added a rushing score. That connection gives Cincinnati every reason to involve Chase early against Atlanta. The Falcons have to account for him while also handling Tee Higgins . Bengals Still Have Another Major Target Tee Higgins arrives in Week 9 as the AFC Offensive Player of the Week. He caught 10 passes for 155 yards against Tennessee and scored twice. Through 7 games, he has 43 catches for 726 yards. His 16.9 yards per catch led the Bengals among their main receivers. home.headline: James Pearce Jr.'s Long-Awaited Return Could Be Longer: Falcons Injury Report
home.blurb: James Pearce Jr.'s Long-Awaited Return Could Be Longer: Falcons Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM Atlanta officially cleared defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. to play, while linebacker Divine Deablo is questionable. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is also questionable after experiencing a setback with his back. Brian Robinson Jr. and Zachariah Branch have been ruled out with hamstring injuries. Pearce is officially listed as questionable, creating some uncertainty around his anticipated return. His potential availability would be important for an Atlanta pass rush looking for additional production against Burrow. His return should provide a boost to Atlanta’s secondary, particularly against a Cincinnati offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow. Bowman has an opportunity to help strengthen a defense that needs to perform better after its struggles against Tampa Bay. Meanwhile, Deablo remains questionable as he attempts to return. Deablo has been dealing with a forearm injury and was limited earlier in the week before returning as a full participant Friday. His progression is an encouraging sign for Atlanta, which has been without the linebacker over the previous two weeks. Robinson, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, remains out for his third straight game. The running back has also missed the last two games. Khalil Herbert will most likely be called to back up Robinson again this week. The Falcons have some encouraging developments heading into their international matchup, particularly with Bowman’s return and Deablo’s progress. However, Pearce’s setback adds another layer of uncertainty to Atlanta’s defensive plans, especially with Samson Ebukam heading to Injurred Reserve. The Atlanta Falcons received some encouraging injury news ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , but there are still several question marks surrounding the team’s availability for Sunday’s international game in Madrid, Spain. The biggest uncertainty, however, could be Pearce. After completing his eight-game suspension, the former first-round pick was expected to make his season debut against Cincinnati. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich previously indicated that Atlanta planned to use Pearce primarily as a pass rusher while monitoring his workload. However, head coach Kevin Stefanski revealed Friday that Pearce experienced a “flare up” in his back injury. The Falcons will monitor how he progresses over the next two days before making a final decision on his availability. Fellow edge rusher Samson Ebukam went to Injured Reserve this week, leaving the Falcons short-handed at the position. Charles Snowden could see more time at edge, and Za'Darius Smith could increase his workload after battling an injury the last several weeks. Another option is inside linebacker Harold Perkins creeping up to an edge spot in pass-rushing situations. Cameron Thomas saw extensive action last week in Tampa with 47 snaps. home.blurb: For fantasy managers, the evidence supports treating Chase as available, and the Week 9 slate offers little reason to sit him. The final inactive report remains the last confirmation before kickoff, and no verified report currently suggests a restriction. The bigger problem sits with Atlanta. Higgins is coming off a 155-yard afternoon, and Chase just produced 141 yards of his own. Burrow has thrown 20 touchdowns through seven games. If the full group is available Sunday, the Falcons have to defend a passing attack that spreads the ball without moving away from its top receiver. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Reveals Bengals WR's Status Before Falcons Matchup By Nishat | November 4, 2026 | Featured , NFL Ja'Marr Chase enters Week 9 in Madrid off the best receiving afternoon of his season. He caught 11 passes for 141 yards in the Cincinnati Bengals ‘ 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans , and he found the end zone in that same game. The only open question was whether the short turnaround to Spain changed anything. Cincinnati's latest injury report answered it. Chase is not listed on the Week 9 injury report. Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update Gives Bengals WR Clear Status The Bengals left Chase off their Wednesday report entirely. That report was only an estimate because the team held a walkthrough instead of a full practice, but it did not carry any new designation for the club's top receiver. Chase also made the trip. He traveled with the team to Madrid on Tuesday, and Bengals.com published a travel photo identifying him among the players on board ahead of the league's international weekend against the Atlanta Falcons . That leaves no verified reason to describe Chase as injured. The report instead points toward normal availability, though the inactive list will not be final until game day. The Week 8 outing was his strongest of the season. Chase caught 11 of 16 targets for 141 yards against the Titans, with a 30-yard long and one trip to the end zone. His 16 targets were a season high. The performance pushed his 2026 totals to 43 catches for 492 yards, and he has six touchdowns through seven games, according to NFL statistics. Joe Burrow played one of his strongest games of the season as well. He completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards against Tennessee. He threw five passing touchdowns in that game and added a rushing score. That connection gives Cincinnati every reason to involve Chase early against Atlanta. The Falcons have to account for him while also handling Tee Higgins . Bengals Still Have Another Major Target Tee Higgins arrives in Week 9 as the AFC Offensive Player of the Week. He caught 10 passes for 155 yards against Tennessee and scored twice. Through 7 games, he has 43 catches for 726 yards. His 16.9 yards per catch led the Bengals among their main receivers. This will mark his third consecutive game on the sidelines. The Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons are in Madrid, Spain, for what should be a memorable international showdown on Sunday. Without Robinson Jr. over the last two games, Atlanta's other running backs, primarily Khalil Herbert, have produced little to nothing. Robinson Jr.'s 2026 Season With Falcons Robinson Jr. is in his fifth NFL season and first with the Falcons. He has played in six games this year. He has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 4.0 yards per carry. That's solid production for a backup running back who rarely gets opportunities because Bijan handles most of the workload. Robinson Jr. spent the first three years of his career with the Washington Commanders after a stellar collegiate career at Alabama. That said, Stefanski added the Falcons will use the rest of this week to determine how many snaps Pearce gets this Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals." Wide receiver Zachariah Branch sat out as expected with a hamstring injury. Stefanski has already ruled the rookie return man out for Sunday's game. Branch was the only player to log a "DNP" on Wednesday, though. home.headline: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8)
home.blurb: Is Baker Mayfield Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). home.headline: Latest Dallas Cowboys injury report brings worrying news for a banged-up defense ahead of Week 9 matchup with Colts
home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys are running out of healthy bodies in the secondary with the Indianapolis Colts coming to town. And a key defender popped up on the injury report out of nowhere. When Porter Jr. was a participant on Wednesday, those concerns eased a bit. On Thursday, however, the Cowboys listed him as a limited participant again. Speaking of the secondary, safeties Caleb Downs and PJ Locke remain in the concussion protocol. Each was upgraded from a non-participant on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday. NFL players who enter the protocol often miss at least one week, but there's no set minimum number of days a player has to sit. In 2023, CBS Sports insider Jonathan Jones reported that the median return from a concussion is nine days. At least Downs and Locke took a significant step forward by getting back to on-field activity as limited participants. Sticking with the defense, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is a new addition to the report. He wasn't listed on Wednesday, but he was limited on Thursday with a hamstring/back injury. Overshown didn't play from Week 1 against the New York Giants until he returned against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. Seeing him back on the injury report isn't encouraging. It doesn't necessarily mean he'll be out on Sunday. As for the rest of the linebacker group, Dee Winters continues to trend in the right direction. He was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday’s practice and is in line to return to the active roster. Wide receiver George Pickens remains on the report after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday. He's now listed with only a hamstring injury, not a shoulder injury. At tight end, Luke Schoonmaker was limited again on Thursday. He missed the last game against the Cardinals with a groin injury, and his status for Week 9 might matter more than expected. Jake Ferguson missed his second straight practice of the week after getting hurt early against Arizona. Elsewhere, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence and returner KaVontae Turpin were non-participants. Offensive tackle Tyler Smith was limited on both Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury, but the Cowboys didn't appear concerned about his availability for Week 9. home.headline: Week 9 Injury Report: Colts Could Catch a Break Against Cowboys
home.blurb: Limited Participants - TE Drew Ogletree (knee) Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. None of the three absences appears particularly concerning, and all should be in a good position to play Sunday barring an unexpected setback. Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. Gould is still required to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before returning to game action, but his progress is an encouraging sign. Boettcher's potential return would be particularly helpful for a linebacker group dealing with some uncertainty. Tight end Drew Ogletree also showed some progress, moving from a DNP designation Wednesday to limited participation Thursday. His availability remains unclear, but the progression is a positive development. Limited Participants - DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) - S P.J. Locke III (concussion) - LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) - WR George Pickens (hamstring) - CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) - TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin) - OG Tyler Smith (ankle) The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker. The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday. Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis. At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded. The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday.

Only the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans won’t play in Week 9, giving bettors and fantasy players plenty of options to choose from in Survivor – if you’ve made it this far. In Week 8, the Dallas Cowboys were the one team that really hurt Survivor players, as they lost as a touchdown favorite at home against a frisky Arizona Cardinals team. Unfortunately for the SI Betting team, Dallas was one of the two teams that we gave out for last week's picks. MacMillan is getting the chance to buy back in so we can offer some differing opinions in Week 9 and upsets across the NFL in the last few weeks have decimated many Survivor Pools. In Week 9, our team is looking to two teams that are favored by six or more points, including Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs after a tough loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. The Chiefs may not be as explosive as they once were, but on their home field they'll cruise past the Jets and help us advance our survivor entries to Week 10. – Iain MacMillan Dallas Cowboys I know the Dallas Cowboys and their terrible defense absolutely crushed Survivor Players (including our own Iain MacMillan) in Week 8, but I’m willing to go back to them on the road in a must-win game against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. The Dallas defense can’t stop anyone, ranking 32nd in EPA/Play and 30th in yards per play allowed, but this offense is still elite. The Cowboys put up 30 points once again in Week 8 against Arizona, and they’re a top-10 team in EPA/Play and success rate on that side of the ball. Dak Prescott should be able to move the ball pretty easily against a Colts defense that couldn’t slow down Trevor Lawrence (three passing scores) and the Jaguars in Week 8. Indy is an easy team to fade the rest of the season with Daniel Jones clearly in over his head at quarterback. Jones has five touchdown passes, nine picks and has only completed 60.4 percent of his passes. If Dallas can’t win this game, the NFC East crown may truly be out of reach. I’ll take the Cowboys – who are six-point road favorites – to bounce back on Sunday. – Peter Dewey Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and approaching the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. picks.headline: Chiefs-Jets betting line & game prediction: KC looks to get back on track
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs enter Sunday as 9.5-point favorites against the Jets at Arrowhead. Kansas City seeks to revive its ground game behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. The prediction picks the Chiefs to beat the Jets 24-13 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs and New York Jets both need a win. Last week, the Chiefs suffered their second straight loss as the Denver Broncos rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to win 28-24. The Jets suffered their third consecutive loss Sunday, falling 38-33 to the Las Vegas Raiders. How to watch Chargers at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Time Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -9.5. Behind the NYJ-KC matchup Although their goals and expectations entering the season were different, Sunday’s Chiefs-Jets game represents a fork in the road for both teams. The Chiefs entered 2026 hoping to rebound from a 6-11 season and return to the Super Bowl conversation, but their loss to Denver has turned simply winning the division into a dogfight. At the same time, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show tangible progress in his second season — or his tenure in New York could be short-lived. A home matchup against the two-win Jets presents the Chiefs with the classic get-right opportunity. Their best path to doing so lies in reestablishing the ground game. New York is 21st in the league against the run in opponent yards per game (123.6), allowing 4.0 yards per carry. During his first five games, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker averaged 133 rushing yards per game. Walker rushed for just 105 yards combined in the losses to Seattle and Denver, but he still ranks third in the NFL with 770 rushing yards. Kansas City will also look for ways to involve rookie Emmett Johnson more after his breakout performance of 143 scrimmage yards against the Broncos. “He’s a super-talented player, and he just brings joy,” quarterback Patrick Mahomes said of Johnson. “He has the right mindset, the right energy, and he wants to be great. Obviously, we have Kenneth, and he’s such a special football player — but to have someone that can come in whenever Kenneth’s tired or needs a break at all, and he can bring energy and juice, too, I think that’s a special combination those guys have there.” Mahomes suggested the Chiefs need to find additional touches for Johnson, potentially through an expanded role in the passing game. Johnson’s 73-yard receiving touchdown highlighted Mahomes’ 321-yard, three-touchdown performance in the loss. Kansas City’s passing game also saw a breath of fresh air with wide receiver Rashee Rice’s return to the lineup. Rice caught a team-high seven passes on eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He also appeared to have the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter before the play was nullified by a false-start penalty . Reestablishing the ground game with Walker and Johnson could create opportunities for Rice, tight end Travis Kelce and wide receiver Xavier Worthy against a veteran Jets secondary that has recorded just one interception this season. Still, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid respects Glenn’s defensive scheme and personnel. “They’ve got some good veteran guys — whether it’s the safeties, the linebackers,” Reid said. “So you’re not going to have things that are botched up. Sometimes, you get coverages that are kind of messed up a little bit and there are holes there. They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. And they’ve got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys.” A Jets player to watch is rookie pass rusher David Bailey, who missed his team’s Week 8 game because of a groin injury. Bailey leads the Jets with 5.5 sacks, more than a quarter of the team’s 20 sacks this season. Reid said there’s a “good chance” left guard Kingsley Suamataia returns to the starting lineup after being benched for the second time in four games because of a “coach’s decision.” The Chiefs’ short-yardage and goal-to-go woes have been under criticism this week after a loss in Denver could have been different by dialing up a quarterback sneak. Perhaps this is the week Reid adds it back into the playbook at long last. Despite New York’s disappointing season, quarterback Geno Smith has put together his own resurgence, entering Sunday with 1,913 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. Smith has posted a passer rating above 100 in five of his last six road games, and the Jets have gained 377 and 439 yards of offense in their past two games. Against a quarterback playing so efficiently, the Chiefs will need to generate more pressure than they did against the Broncos. Pro Football Focus credited Kansas City with just five pressures against Denver’s Bo Nix. While wide receiver Garrett Wilson’s status remains in concussion protocol, running back Breece Hall could return after missing five games. In Hall’s absence, Braelon Allen has been a fantastic replacement, recording at least 100 scrimmage yards in the last four consecutive games. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, acquired by New York from Indianapolis in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts, established a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Raiders. Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane missed Sunday’s game after aggravating his shoulder injury but returned to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday. Delane’s return is more important given Smith has been brilliant at throwing the deep ball, with 565 yards gained on passes of 20-plus air yards. Defensive end George Karlaftis said Wednesday that coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has preached the importance of developing a “killer instinct” after his unit’s forgettable recent fourth quarter. “No matter what the call is, you just got to find a way to finish,” Karlaftis said. “So I think, especially against a divisional opponent, against a great team that Denver is, when you’re up, when you’re leading, no matter what that lead is, you got to find a way to win the game as a defense. “And I know I felt that. I know the guys in the room, players and coaches, really felt that. And I think that’s something we’re going to take with us and harp on for the rest of the season.” Reid confirmed Wednesday that Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs’ kicker against the Jets despite his 54-yard miss against Denver. Butker had made three extra points and a 45-yard field goal before pushing his final kick wide right. The Chiefs can get back on the right path and build some confidence by handling the Jets. The problems — an inconsistent pass rush, short-yardage struggles and too many penalties — have been glaring. This is a good opponent to fix all three against. Jets-Chiefs game prediction Beyond the Chiefs’ advantages in record, quarterback and overall outlook, I think this matchup gives Kansas City an opportunity to tap back into the offensive identity that worked early in the season — establishing Walker on the ground to open up everything else. Defensively, clean up the penalties and get to the quarterback. We’ve heard plenty about pressures, but Smith has been sacked 23 times this season — tied for second-most in the NFL. If not Sunday against the Jets, then when? The Chiefs use their get-right game to do just that. away.blurb: The New York Jets could be without their No. 1 wide receiver weapon in Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. When speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced that Garrett Wilson is in the NFL ‘s concussion protocol and considered “day-to-day” moving forward. “Garrett, he’s in the concussion protocol. Additionally, Miami did not notch its first win of the season until Week 7, defeating Aaron Glenn and the N.Y. Jets, 28-25. Undeniably, it's been a rough season for Hafley & Co., which find themselves in possession of the third-worst record in the NFL. The only teams which have been worse are the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the L.A. Chargers (0-7). The Lions, under Dan Campbell, were once in the same unenviable shoes as the Dolphins. When Campbell first took over in the Motor City in 2021, Detroit was far from one of the most formidable teams in the NFL. Instead, just like the Dolphins currently, Campbell & Co. experienced their fair share of struggles and lost plenty of games on their way to establishing their tough, gritty identity. In fact, Detroit started the aforementioned campaign 0-10-1 before winning its first game in Week 13 against the Minnesota Vikings. In that sense, Campbell sees plenty of parallels between those Lions and this current iteration of Miami. “Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” the sixth-year Lions head man expressed to reporters this week. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.” As much as Campbell's squad is undoubtedly the better team, you can't take anyone lightly in the NFL. And for as bad as the Dolphins have been, it's important to note they have not lost a game by more than seven points since Week 4. Their last double-digit loss came in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs (24-10). And on top of all that, the Lions are severely banged up entering this Week 9 matchup , after suffering a plethora of injuries a week ago against Minnesota. They lost five total defensive players in the divisional tilt, including defensive captain Jack Campbell, the two best members of their secondary (Brian Branch and D.J. Reed) and EDGE DJ Wonnum. And they all are in danger of missing Detroit’s interconference contest in Miami. As a result, Miami – led under center by fifth-year passer Malik Willis – might have a chance to do some damage against Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit . Yet, the Lions are seven-point favorites, per multiple sportsbooks, for a reason, and should emerge victorious in the road affair. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 72 percent chance to secure the Week 9 victory .
