While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they've strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Dolphins - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Dolphins Oct 30, 2022; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) makes a pass against Miami Dolphins during the second half at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Junfu Han-USA TODAY Sports Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) will face off in Week 9 in a battle between two teams at different stages in their regime builds. The Lions have their eyes firmly set on the postseason and are riding a three-game win streak, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and are performing much like the Lions did in 2021 and 2022—lots of grit, but struggling to find success. "(Dolphins Head) Coach (Jeff) Hafley's done a good job in his first year," Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Wednesday. "A lot of similarities to—just reminds me a little of what we were when we came in. They're young, they're hungry, they're active. They run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball, and they're playing that way." This week's prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +1600 to win this year's Super Bowl and are currently 7-point favorites in Week 9 . Let's take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Dolphins in this week's Honolulu Blueprint. Dolphin s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 9 preview: Breaking down the Dolphins' offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Lions slow down pass rush with runs up the middle Last Sunday, the Lions faced arguably the best defense in the NFL when they went head-to-head with the Vikings, and while the Dolphins are on the opposite end of the rankings spectrum, some of the strategies the Lions used against Minnesota will transfer over to this week's game against Miami. The Dolphins defense enters this game 29th in DVOA, 24th in points allowed (25.9), 24th in yards allowed per play (5.7 ypp), and are dead last in the NFL in three areas: EPA per play (+0.10), EPA per pass allowed (+0.26), and passing yards allowed per play (8.3). However, this defense is showing growth in pressure rate. Looking at season totals, the Dolphins' pressure numbers could be a bit deceiving: 31st in total pressures (77), 18th in pressure rate (35.6%), 30th in total sacks (9), and 28th in sack rate (4.2%). But when you look at the splits from their last four games, you can see the improvement: at Vikings: 17 pressures, 39.5% pressure rate, 4 sacks, 9.3% sack rate vs. Bengals: 11 pressures, 33.3% pressure rate, 0 sacks, 0% sack rate at Jets: 15 pressures, 45.5% pressure rate, 2 sacks, 6.1% sack rate vs. Patriots: 13 pressures, 48.1% pressure rate, 3 sacks, 11.1% sack rate If we isolate the games against the Vikings, Jets, and Patriots, we see nearly 60% of the defensive pressures and 100% of the Dolphins sacks. When you look at how the Dolphins have generated pressures and sacks, most of those situations come from stunting their defensive linemen. Last week against the Patriots, the Dolphins sacked the quarterback once on an end-of-half situation, with the other two sacks coming off a stunt where an edge rusher loops behind the interior defensive lineman and twists inside. We also saw stunts get home against the Vikings in Week 4. To counter the Dolphins' stunts, offenses have been attacking the middle of the defensive line with their rushing attacks; teams are running inside 53% of the time, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. While the Lions have preferred to lean on their outside-zone rushing scheme, we saw last week against the Vikings that Detroit has a formula to get downhill on inside runs. Now, the Lions don't necessarily need to deploy a full-house set (three players in the backfield) again, but it would certainly be effective against the Dolphins' Wide-9 base 4-3 defense. Prediction 2: Lions cross the zone to open the field for Goff While all defenses are complex, at their core, the Dolphins split their defensive personnel almost evenly between a base 4-3 (three linebackers) front and a "Big Nickel" (three safeties) formation. Regardless of set, they spend about 80% of the time in zone coverage, with half of that time spent between single-high (Cover-1, -3) and two-high (Cover-2, -4, -6) safety sets. When they deploy man coverage, they run exclusively single-high Cover-1. Depending on the safety formation, Lions quarterback Jared Goff will have to find the holes in the zone to exploit, but those gaps can widen if the Lions stretch the Dolphins laterally with their passing game. Based on the games I watched, the Dolphins' defenders settle in their zones and tend to be slow to react to crossing routes in front of them. When offenses find success on crossers and stretch the zones across the field, that opens gaps down the deep seams, where speed receivers—hey, Jameson Williams—have found chunk plays. If the Lions can slow the Dolphins' pass rush with run up the middle, then stretch the secondary laterally, they'll have an opportunity to chew up yards in a variety of ways. Prediction 3: Lions match physicality; prevent explosive runs When the Dolphins lost their dynamic running back De'Von Achane to an ACL injury in Week 3, many thought Miami's rushing attack would struggle. However, second-year back Ollie Gordon has stepped into a starting role, and the Dolphins' new downhill, physical rushing attack has proved to be an asset, even outproducing their early-season statistics, save last week vs. the Patriots. With quarterback Malik Willis adding another element to the run game through RPOs and scrambles, stopping the run will likely be the Lions' top priority. On paper, their raw numbers look good: rushing for 123.3 yards per game (11th), averaging 4.4 yards per carry (11th), -0.03 EPA per rush (10th), 26 runs that gain 10+ yards (7th), and explosive runs 16.7% (3rd). However, there are some concerning numbers that point to struggles with consistency, including: Rushing DVOA: 26th Rushing success rate: 38.7% (20th) Stuffed rate: 20% (26th) Adjusted line yards: 3.64 (27th) The Dolphins will want to establish their rushing attack against the Lions, and Detroit will need to match that downhill physicality. It wouldn't be surprising to see the Lions spend a lot of time in base early as both teams work to control the trenches. Expect seven and eight defenders in the box pre-snap, and a situational spy to track Willis is likely. With changes coming to the Lions' linebacker roles, Detroit will need Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, and Malcolm Rodriguez to elevate their games and keep the explosive runs in check. Prediction 4: Lions pass rushers get after Willis If the Dolphins can establish the run, they do a nice job of running play-action behind it and finding success. But that's not always an option for Miami's offense, and the inconsistencies in the run game have forced Willis to create opportunities on his own. Willis is talented—we saw that in Green Bay—comfortable passing from the pocket, and able to extend plays by escaping outside. But with limited support, he holds onto the ball too long, takes sacks, or misses his targets because his accuracy gets loose/inconsistent on the run. Miami's offensive line is average at best (see below) and doesn't hold up well against pressure, and while the Dolphins receivers have unique skills, they lack a true playmaker and currently rely on two rookies—Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell—in starting wide receiver roles. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. home.blurb: The Miami Dolphins may be rebuilding, but that does not mean every veteran needs a departure ticket. As Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline approaches, Zach Sieler’s future comes down to a familiar question. Would the return outweigh the value of keeping a captain who wants to help Miami win? Breer also reported that the Dolphins “aren’t hanging up on anyone.” That leaves room for an exceptional offer, but it does not make Sieler a player Miami is actively shopping. No verified offer, agreed compensation package or confirmed destination appears in the available reporting. It makes sense to listen to anything. If someone is giving away the farm, you should probably take it. On Tuesday, November 10th, the NFL Trade Deadline hits. Teams have been planning and scurrying to fill holes, find the player that will put them over the hump to make a playoff run or perhaps shed salaries to rebuild once again. That’s not the case in South Beach. History of Sieler Trade Interest Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer offered the clearest indication of Miami’s position just last week on Oct. 30. “Miami has gotten interest in DT Zach Sieler and C Aaron Brewer , but quickly rebuffed that, and sees those two and Jordyn Brooks as important influences on their raft of rookies.” But the veteran has been on the Dolphin raft and seen the tide rise this season even though the scoreboard isn’t an indicator of that at 1-6. Sieler’s own position is emphatic. “I know people say rumors or talk whatever this time of year, but I’m here focused playing games here, win as a Dolphin, man.” He added. “I love it here. I’ve been here for how long? I want to win here as a Dolphin. I think (Head Coach Jeff) Hafley, (General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan) Sully have done an amazing job here.” He has not requested a trade. Agent Drew Rosenhaus would be “shocked” if Sieler were dealt, according to the Palm Beach Post and Pro Football Rumors. For coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, keeping Miami’s longest-tenured player offers continuity as younger teammates navigate a difficult season. No Need To Sell – The Future Looks Bright – Hang On At 1-6, Miami has reasons to consider future assets. But ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reported that the Dolphins “won’t be locked into selling, either” and would need “strong offers” to move players such as Sieler and offensive tackle Austin Jackson , who are considered leaders in their position groups. Sieler, 31, is under contract through 2029, so Miami is not trying to salvage value from an expiring deal. His $1.3 million base salary makes him relatively inexpensive for a buyer this season, while a $10 million injury guarantee for 2027 that vests in March creates another decision point beyond Tuesday. picks.headline: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints
picks.blurb: 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms 3 Bold predictions for the Browns in Week 9 against the Saints Jeffrey Olson, Browns Wire · Browns Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:55 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are looking to keep pace in the playoff race this weekend. They will have to beat the 2-5 New Orleans Saints to do that and hopefully gain some ground in the AFC North. This is a winnable game, and to expect the Browns to win is not a bold opinion. If you want some sort of bold prediction, then we have those too. A forecast that goes beyond that of normal expectations, but also stays in the realm of reality. Here are my three bold predictions for the Browns against the Saints. KC Concepcion rushing score The Saints do not have a good run defense (ranked 29th in rushing yards allowed). I expect the Browns to lean heavily into their running game. This would be especially true if backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders is starting. I expect that Concepcion will be very involved in the passing game. I also think the Browns will look for creative ways to get him touches considering how elusive and explosive he is. Don't be surprised if he finds the end zone on an end-around or a backward pass type play. Judkins goes off I won't go as far as to say that Quinshon Judkins will have his best day of the year because I don't think he outdoes what he did versus the Titans. However, I don't think this game will be way off from that in terms of production. As stated before, the Saints have a bad run defense. It makes sense to take the ball out of the hands of a backup quarterback and run the ball early and often. Look for a 100-yard day and a score from Judkins. Shough-ing turnovers There is no debate that the Browns defense has been their strength this year. They rank 13th in points allowed per game and 13th in total turnovers forced. This pairs with the Browns' advantage, as the Saints are 6th in the NFL in most giveaways. I won't go as far as to predict a turnover fiesta this weekend, but I will predict that Saints Quarterback Tyler Shough has at least two in this game. The Browns are currently in third place within the AFC North division, with the team still thinking about a possible playoff run. While the loss to the Steelers was very disappointing for the Browns, the team still has the utmost confidence as it enters the game this week. However, the Browns will likely be playing the game with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders, with starter Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion. It remains to be seen if Sanders will be starting the game, but at this point, it's trending toward happening . Sanders did play last season for the Browns, going 3-4 as a starter at the end of the year. As for New Orleans, they will be coming into the game with a record of 2-5 on the season, but the team did have a bye this past week. New Orleans has gone 0-4 at home this year, giving the Browns some extra ammo going into the week. Experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report predicted how the contest would go this week. Among these picks, only two of the seven chose Cleveland to go on the road to win this week. O'Donnell and Sobleski were the two to choose the Browns to grab the win this week over the Saints. Cleveland's defense has the talent to keep them in this game, but the offense is likely going to have to win it. For the Browns, whoever is under center will be tasked with getting this team back on track. The offense has sputtered over the last few weeks, and this is an area that Cleveland wants to get back going strong. New Orleans can be a sneaky team, even with their lackluster record on the season, with them having beaten the Baltimore Ravens, with a healthy Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and New York Giants this year. The Saints were expected to be better than where they currently are, so the Browns will need to be careful. Kickoff for this game will take place at 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans.

away.headline: Cleveland Browns Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Cleveland Browns have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. The Browns will be without Jenkins for their Week 8 game against the Steelers, and he's required to miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. For Week 8, the Browns are relatively healthy, with only two players listed as questionable: cornerback Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas . Harden suffered a hamstring injury during the Browns' Week 7 but returned to the game. He was limited in practice throughout the week and is questionable against Pittsburgh. Thomas was also limited throughout the week with an ankle injury and carries a questionable designation. Howard suffered a concussion during Cleveland's Week 7 win against Tennessee and missed all three practice sessions this week. The Browns initially listed him as questionable on Friday but announced Saturday that he had cleared concussion protocol, which is a big relief considering the strength of Pittsburgh's defensive line. away.blurb: In addition to Fannin being limited, the Browns may be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson for the week. Watson is currently in concussion protocol, and his status for the game against New Orleans remains uncertain. Cleveland will be entering Week 9 of the season with a record of 5-3 on the year, sitting in third place in the AFC North. The Browns have been able to see strong performances from players on both sides of the ball, leading to their success this year. This team will be heading on the road for a big game against the New Orleans Saints, with Cleveland trying to get back on track. However, the Browns are dealing with some key injuries to players ahead of the game. One of those has just popped up on the injury report for Cleveland, with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. dealing with a groin injury. Fannin dealt with a groin injury last season, limiting what he could do on the field and his overall availability. If Fannin is unable to play, it could be a tough break for the Browbs, especially after his breakout game last week . Fannin caught 10 passes for 154 yards against the Steelers, and he was the primary offensive option for the team. On the year, Fannin has been a reliable presence for this team, giving Watson someone to find when needed the most. Overall, the tight end has caught 35 passes for 411 yards and three touchdowns for Cleveland. If Watson can't play, backup Shedeur Sanders will be named the starter for the Browns this week. Sanders was able to get some playing time in last year for Cleveland, giving him some needed experience to man this team forward. At this point, it seems like Sanders will be under center for the Browns against the Saints, barring a major change. Last season, Sanders went 3-4 as a starter for the Browns, throwing for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Sanders and Fannin developed nice chemistry last season when playing together, so if the pass-catcher does miss, it could be tough for the quarterback. But the Browns will hope for the best when it comes to all the injured players as the team prepares for the Saints game.

home.headline: Concerning Browns Player Pops Up on Injury Report Ahead of Saints Game
home.blurb: In addition to Fannin being limited, the Browns may be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson for the week. Watson is currently in concussion protocol, and his status for the game against New Orleans remains uncertain. Concerning Browns Player Pops Up on Injury Report Ahead of Saints Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 Story by Concerning Browns Player Pops Up on Injury Report Ahead of Saints Game Story by Concerning Browns Player Pops Up on Injury Report Ahead of Saints Game (Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:58 p.m. UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns remain one of the bigger surprises in the NFL, despite the team's loss last week against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cleveland will be entering Week 9 of the season with a record of 5-3 on the year, sitting in third place in the AFC North. The Browns have been able to see strong performances from players on both sides of the ball, leading to their success this year. This team will be heading on the road for a big game against the New Orleans Saints, with Cleveland trying to get back on track. However, the Browns are dealing with some key injuries to players ahead of the game. One of those has just popped up on the injury report for Cleveland, with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. dealing with a groin injury. Fannin dealt with a groin injury last season, limiting what he could do on the field and his overall availability. If Fannin is unable to play, it could be a tough break for the Browbs, especially after his breakout game last week . Fannin caught 10 passes for 154 yards against the Steelers, and he was the primary offensive option for the team. On the year, Fannin has been a reliable presence for this team, giving Watson someone to find when needed the most. Overall, the tight end has caught 35 passes for 411 yards and three touchdowns for Cleveland. If Watson can't play, backup Shedeur Sanders will be named the starter for the Browns this week. Sanders was able to get some playing time in last year for Cleveland, giving him some needed experience to man this team forward. At this point, it seems like Sanders will be under center for the Browns against the Saints, barring a major change. Last season, Sanders went 3-4 as a starter for the Browns, throwing for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Sanders and Fannin developed nice chemistry last season when playing together, so if the pass-catcher does miss, it could be tough for the quarterback. But the Browns will hope for the best when it comes to all the injured players as the team prepares for the Saints game.

home.headline: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint
home.blurb: While they might not be out of the divisional race just yet, the Saints really need things to turn around soon, or else this season will end in disappointment. Fortunately, during their bye week, the Saints got some great news on a key injured player. "Saints first-pick Jordyn Tyson could return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him as early as next week vs. the Browns , per sources," Schefter reports. "But even if it's not then, he is not far away from playing." Rushing him back before the bye would've made no sense, especially for a team that's likely still trying to climb out of the bottom of the NFC. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. He suffered a hamstring injury leading up to the regular season, causing him to land on IR. He's since missed seven games, and with the Week 8 bye giving the Saints an early-season week off, it makes sense that Tyson missed those first seven weeks. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense Michael Owens/Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night. It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history. What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions. Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss. However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season. Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008. This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career. Vikings sack Bills QB Josh Allen more than five times Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics: Scoring defense (13.3 points per game allowed) Red zone defense (25% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-line defense (37.5% goal-line touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (56.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (4-8) Sack rate (11%) QB pressure rate (46%) Blitz rate (73.6%, the highest by any team in the 21st century) They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks. Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career. Cowboys hold the Colts to under 20 points The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL. However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season. Jets' Braelon Allen goes off against Chiefs New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548. Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008. Dolphins hold Lions QB Jared Goff to under 200 passing yards The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success. Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25). However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game. The pick: Giants 34, Eagles 20 Here's why: The Eagles are a mess right now and that's a big reason why the Giants are in prime position to win the NFC East. picks.blurb: Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles sacks Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants during the third quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:19 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they've owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed's questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team's turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn't have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn't afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy's playing time has been limited but he's shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don't know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is "excitement." The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don't know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That's hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn't have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Giants' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren't. When they aren't, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they've been favored in Philly since 2009), what's your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I'm still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers responds to concerns after sudden injury update
away.blurb: Nabers held no injury designation earlier this week and was a full participant on Wednesday. However, he logged a “DNP” designation on Thursday’s injury report. New York Giants superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers sparked some concern regarding his health on Thursday, working with trainers off to the side of the practice field. When asked about his lack of practice participation on Thursday, Nabers pumped the breaks on concerns regarding his status for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles. “I’ll be good,” Nabers told reporters. Nabers has been absolutely stellar through the Giants’ last four games, reeling in 36 catches for 509 yards and two touchdowns over that span. On Thursday, the NFL recognized him as the NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. Nabers wasted no time developing chemistry with new quarterback JJ McCarthy. In McCarthy’s first start with the Giants in Week 7, Nabers secured seven of his nine targets for 111 yards in an overtime win over the Houston Texans. Fresh off their Week 8 bye, the Giants will kick off against the Eagles at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. away.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers reveals game status after missing practice
away.blurb: New York Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers sat out of the team’s latest practice on Thursday due to a knee injury. However, he’s confident it won’t sideline him for the Giants Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. According to Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Nabers told reporters that he will be good to go for Sunday’s game. It certainly allows for a sigh of relief as the Giants continue to fend off the rest of the NFC East in first place with a 4-2-1 record. The Dallas Cowboys are in second place at 3-5, Washington Commanders in third at 2-4-1 and Eagles in last at 2-6. There’s no overstating how much Nabers means to New York’s offense as he has already racked up 48 receptions for 605 yards and two touchdowns this season. If Nabers were to ever have to miss any time, the Giants wide receiver corps would become a big concern with rookie Malachi Fields and veterans Darnell Mooney, Charlie Jones and Gunner Olszewski next in line. The Giants are already without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season after he suffered a multi-ligament left knee injury in Week 2, so Nabers has and will continue to play a very big role in elevating the play of whoever is at quarterback. The Giants will issue an official designation for Nabers on Friday, so all eyes will be peeled when that injury report is released. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Nabers has recorded 175 catches for 2,080 yards and 11 touchdowns in his professional career. home.headline: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game
home.blurb: There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle. If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night. NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game Skip to main content SI.COM New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice. Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago. At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.” Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans. Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury. If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game. "I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray). "So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll." While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia. Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring. Although the Commanders' 2-4-1 record is far from impressive, they remain a dangerous team that can win on any given Sunday. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is currently fighting for his job , and injuries have plagued the team throughout a disappointing season. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has missed several games this season after aggravating a previous arm injury, while several other key players have been sidelined for significant periods of time. While they are 2-4-1, the Commanders still have an opportunity to win the weak NFC East. The Commanders just won their second game of the season after defeating the Philadelphia Eagles and currently sit third in the division. This season, the Commanders are 17th in points per game and 26th in points allowed. They have also struggled on third down, converting just 32% of their attempts, while their defense has surrendered too many points. Although the Commanders have been one of the worst teams this season, they have found success running the ball. Led by their dual-threat quarterback, they average 127 rushing yards per game and protect the ball with only three turnovers. The Commanders' biggest weakness lies in their passing defense, which ranks 27th in the league, allowing 243 yards per game and an opponent passer rating of 100.6. The Rams' success largely depends on quarterback Matthew Stafford's ability to effectively move the ball. Stafford is reportedly dealing with soreness in his right arm. He left the locker room after the Chargers game with a bag of ice on his right elbow. This could be a big game for Puka Nacua . Held to only 80 yards in Week 9, Nacua might have over 100 receiving yards this week. The Rams should still find success running the ball, but the overall game will depend on Stafford's effectiveness passing the ball. In a must-win game for the Rams, this news comes at the worst time. Garrett, who was acquired from the Cleveland Browns in June, played in the Rams' season opener, but has been out since after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September . Following the Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, the pass rusher said he wasn't 100% healthy after missing most of training camp with a knee issue. After back-to-back days of being limited in practice, Garrett is reportedly "on track" to play this Sunday when the Rams face the Washington Commanders. Head coach Sean McVay said he did not want to create an expectation for the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year to be close to a return. It was important to see how his knee responded to practice before he could progress to the next step in the recovery process. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Rams working through lengthy injury report before Commanders game
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are dealing with another difficult week on the injury front, and there is still plenty of uncertainty surrounding several key players ahead of their matchup against the Washington Commanders. With a growing list of contributors either limited or absent from practice, Los Angeles is once again navigating the challenge of keeping its roster healthy while attempting to build momentum. The injury report features several notable names, including Myles Garrett (knee), Matthew Stafford (elbow) , Trent McDuffie (back), Kam Curl (foot), Terrance Ferguson (ankle), Steve Avila (hamstring), and Colby Parkinson (ribs). The majority of the report consists of players listed as limited participants or DNP, leaving questions about who will ultimately be available Sunday. Just as the Rams appear to be turning a corner and finding some consistency, another wave of injuries threatens to disrupt their progress. The latest blow came with Jaylen Watson being placed on season-ending injured reserve due to his recurring shoulder issue. Losing another defensive contributor is far from ideal as the team approaches a critical stretch of the schedule post-bye week. There is still optimism surrounding the potential returns of Garrett and Ferguson. Both players could provide significant boosts to their respective units, but the coaching staff is unlikely to push either player back before they are physically ready. Getting them healthy for the long term remains more important than rushing their availability for one game. McDuffie's situation is also worth monitoring closely. The Rams are hoping his back issue does not force him to miss additional time, especially considering he has already been sidelined for two games this season. Ultimately, Los Angeles needs some positive injury news. The Rams have the talent to compete, but staying healthy is becoming an increasingly difficult obstacle to overcome.

picks.headline: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos?
picks.blurb: Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Week 9 Preview: Can the Carolina Panthers Keep Up With the Denver Broncos? | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Sue Levine, Editor Christopher Mason · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers are coming off a mini-bye week following their Thursday night football loss to the Green Bay Packers . Now, they prepare to welcome one of the AFC's top teams, the Denver Broncos . Denver travels to Charlotte following a close win against its division rival, the Kansas City Chiefs. This will be the ninth meeting between the two teams, with the Broncos holding a 7-2 advantage over Carolina, including their victory in Super Bowl 50. The Panthers enter this matchup barely holding on to their first-place lead in the NFC South and riding a two-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Broncos sit comfortably atop the AFC West and look to extend their lead against a struggling Carolina team. Both teams have their own issues. Carolina's defense has looked like a shell of itself while dealing with injuries and coaching changes. Denver's offense, meanwhile, has struggled to find consistency in the early stages of games, often waiting until the second half to hit its stride. Although the teams' records suggest a mismatch, this game presents an interesting study in how teams start versus how they finish. Green Bay Packers linebacker Ty'ron Hopper (59) is stiff-armed by Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard (30) on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 27-19. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Denver's Offense vs. Carolina's Defense The Denver Broncos are very much a second-half team, with their offense becoming more productive as games progress. Denver has generated 1,066 yards of total offense in the first half compared with 1,110 in the second half. The difference becomes more pronounced in the passing game, where the Broncos have recorded seven second-half passing touchdowns compared with just two in the first half. Bo Nix's yards per attempt also increased to 6.6 after halftime. The Panthers cannot afford to let Denver find its rhythm through the air. One way to prevent that is by generating consistent pressure on Nix, who has struggled against opposing blitzes. Carolina has had difficulty getting after the quarterback this season, with injuries taking a toll on its edge-rushing group. If the Panthers can disrupt Nix in the pocket, they could interrupt the rhythm that has allowed Denver to become more productive in the second half. Carolina must also find a way to stop the run. It is a message Coach Dave Canales has emphasized to new defensive coordinator Todd Wash . The Panthers have struggled against opposing rushing attacks, allowing approximately 140 yards per game on the ground. Denver uses its rushing attack to create favorable passing opportunities for Nix by forcing opposing safeties closer to the line of scrimmage. Running back Jonah Coleman also brings the speed to create problems for Carolina's defense at the second level. The Panthers showed some improvement against Green Bay, holding the Packers to fewer than 100 rushing yards while generating penetration from defensive tackles Lee Hunter and Derrick Brown. If Carolina can force Denver's running backs to deal with linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke, the Broncos could have a more difficult time creating the deep passing opportunities Nix prefers. Establishing control of the line of scrimmage will be critical to keeping Denver's offense in check. Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Lee Hunter (92) and linebacker Bobby Okereke (58) during warmups against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Can Carolina's Secondary Stop Bo Nix? The Carolina Panthers' secondary faces a productive touchdown scorer in Bo Nix. However, the Denver quarterback enters this matchup with some concerning passing efficiency numbers. Nix is averaging 6 yards per attempt while completing approximately 60% of his passes. He has also thrown nine touchdowns against three interceptions. His 83.6 passer rating further highlights some of the inconsistencies in Denver's passing attack. Those numbers present an opportunity for Carolina's secondary to disrupt the Broncos' aerial game. The Panthers will need to force Nix into difficult throws and make him take risks when attempting to push the ball downfield. However, Nix is particularly effective at extending plays and creating open passing lanes with his mobility in the pocket. Carolina's inability to generate a consistent pass rush could work in Denver's favor. If the Panthers cannot pressure Nix, he will have additional time to find receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle downfield. However, if Carolina's secondary can stay with Denver's receivers, Nix may be forced to extend plays and search for alternative passing windows. The Panthers must force Nix into difficult throwing angles and prevent him from creating open passing lanes over the middle of the field. Doing so could limit Denver's explosive plays while disrupting the timing of its offense. The longer Nix has to hold the football while searching for an open receiver, the more opportunities Carolina's defense will have to make a play. Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Bryce Young vs. the Broncos' Defense The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against Denver's defense. The Broncos enter this matchup tied for fourth in the NFL with 23 sacks. Bryce Young was sacked six times last week and has taken 11 sacks over the past two games. Young struggled to recognize pressure against Green Bay, while Carolina's offensive line consistently had difficulty giving him enough time to operate. This week, the Panthers' offensive line will have to contend with Nik Bonitto, Jonathan Cooper, and Zach Allen. All three have been among Denver's leading sack producers this season and have established themselves as key disruptors along the defensive front. Carolina will need to find ways to work around Denver's pass rush. That means incorporating quick passes, getting the football into the hands of its playmakers, and establishing a more consistent rushing attack. The Panthers do not have an elite running game, but Chuba Hubbard has shown the ability to break off explosive runs when given the opportunity. If Carolina can get Hubbard going early, it could open up the passing game, particularly through play-action. Carolina will also need to get creative with its receiver alignments. Tetairoa McMillan will likely see plenty of Denver's premier cornerback, Pat Surtain II. The Panthers should move McMillan around the formation to create more favorable matchups and prevent Denver from consistently deploying Surtain against Carolina's leading receiver. Similarly, if Jalen Coker is healthy enough to play at full strength, Carolina's receiving duo could give Denver some problems. Having multiple receiving threats available would make it more difficult for the Broncos to focus their coverage on McMillan. Ultimately, Young needs to get the football out quickly, avoid unnecessary sacks, and take advantage of the opportunities Denver's defense gives him. Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images The Last Word The Carolina Panthers will have their hands full against a tough opponent this week. While Carolina is struggling to keep its head above water, last week's game showed glimpses of the team fans had seen earlier in the season. The Panthers made a late push against Green Bay, fighting until the final seconds despite being outplayed for much of the night. If Carolina can keep Nix in check by forcing him to extend plays, disrupting his passing rhythm, and containing Denver's rushing attack, the defense could give the offense more opportunities to compete. On the offensive side of the ball, offensive coordinator Brad Idzik needs to return to some of the principles that made Carolina's offense successful earlier in the season. Establishing the run will go a long way toward opening up opportunities for the receivers while giving Young more time to make the throws he needs. If Carolina can execute complementary football and Todd Wash's defense shows signs of improvement under its new leadership, the Panthers could make this a competitive matchup. However, beating Denver will require four quarters of consistent football. Carolina cannot afford another slow start or a second-half collapse. Against a team that has made a habit of getting better as games progress, the Panthers will need to put together their most complete performance in weeks. Panthers (3-4) at Bank of America Stadium. Although their record is a game below .500, the Panthers are also a first place team as they sit atop the NFC South. The Broncos have won four straight since a loss in early October at San Francisco. Carolina has suffered lopsided defeats in each of their last two games. This past Sunday, Bo Nix and the Broncos staged an impressive comeback to beat Kansas City, 28-24. Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before Nix found Nate Adkins for a touchdown and Jaylen Waddle for the two-point conversion. After a missed Chiefs’ field goal, Nix connected with rookie Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, setting up Coleman’s go-ahead five-yard touchdown with 1:56 remaining. Denver then preserved the victory when its defense stopped Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on fourth-and-goal. Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Denver has now won 15 one-score games over the past two seasons. As mentioned, Carolina has lost two straight, most recently losing at Green Bay last Thursday 27-19. The Panthers actually led 10-6 early in the second quarter behind a Chuba Hubbard touchdown, but Green Bay answered with 21 straight points to take control. Bryce Young completed 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Hubbard supplied 81 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries plus seven catches for 38 yards. Carolina made things interesting when Young hit Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown with 5:37 left, but the Panthers failed on the two-point conversion and never scored again. The most troubling stats to emerge from the game was Young being sacked six times and Carolina’s offense managing only 258 yards. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: S Brandon Jones trending toward inactive
away.blurb: Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers. Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction. Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina. In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady. WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury. On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos. Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs . Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9. “You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.” Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. away.headline: Broncos injuries: Zach Allen and 3 others cleared to play
away.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. NFL Week 9 Preview: Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers
picks.blurb: Search News Open dropdown menu Latest News Food & Drink Open dropdown menu Latest Food & Drink Restaurant Reviews Openings & Closings Food & Drink Events Arts & Pop Culture Open dropdown menu Latest Arts & Pop Culture Music Open dropdown menu Latest Music Concert Calendar Things To Do Open dropdown menu Latest Things To Do Events Calendar Best of Houston® Open dropdown menu Best of Houston® 2025 Best of Houston® 2024 Best of Houston® 2023 Best of Houston® Archives List an Event Advertise with Us Close Our History Menu Instagram Houston Press The Leading Independent News Source in Houston, Texas Search for: Search Menu News Open dropdown menu Latest News Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email When the Houston Texans’ schedule was released back in May, we looked at all the game on the slate, and looked at where and when they would all be played. When the Los Angeles Chargers landed in Week 9, hosting the Texans at SoFi Stadium, I think most fans and media looked at that matchup as one of the most even matchups on the board, a game that could go either way. Nine weeks into the season, anyone who thought that is, in actuality, correct, but I doubt that anyone who viewed this game as an even matchups back in September figured it would be even because both teams stink. After all, these are two teams who reached the postseason the last two seasons. Instead, both teams are a combined 2-12. In short, these are two bad, underachieving squads. Make no mistake, this is a bigger game for the Texans than it is for the Chargers. The Chargers’ season is essentially over. They’re more worried about making sure their quarterback, who makes $55 million per year, isn’t broken, than they are worried about out the postseason. The Texans still harbor faint playoff hopes, and losing to a winless, rudderless mess like the Chargers would take the low point of the DeMeco Ryans Era, which is where we are right now, and plunge it into the center of the earth. This is a must-win for the Texans, flat out. Here are four things to watch for this weekend in this game: 4. What exactly got fixed during the bye week? As Coach Ryans pointed out in multiple media appearances over the last two weeks, there were no shortage of areas to reassess and focus on improvement. The Texans have been among the worst tackling teams in football, and probably not coincidentally, they did what Will Anderson described as “pee wee ball” tackling drills on Wednesday. The Texans have been among the most penalized teams in football. I’m not sure how a bye week fixes that, but it needs fixing. Communication on defense has been a major culprit in the Texans’ allowing the highest number of explosive plays in the NFL. This also must get fixed. Finally, play selection and play calling have been inconsistent and flat out bizarre at times. Ryans indicated they had meetings to address that, as well. The proof will be in the play on Sunday. 3. Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison, Jr. During the bye week, the Texans placed wide receiver Jaylin Noel on injured reserve with a toe injury. He is done for the year. Fortunately, Tank Dell returned just before the bye week, and with some noticeable overlap in skill set with Noel, Dell is likely ready to assume some of Noel’s workload. Additionally, Harrison, the Texans’ big trade acquisition in October, has played just a few snaps in each of his first two games as a Texan. That needs to change, especially if the Texans are looking to recoup the value of the second round pick they sent to Arizona in exchange for Harrison. Finally, Nico Collins needs to flat out be on the field more than he was against the Giants, where he played barely 60 percent of the snaps. This wide receiver room has talent, and it’s up to OC Nick Caley to deploy it, and stop running these “jumbo” packages with six offensive linemen. 2. Justin Herbert’s slow meltdown into football hell If you listen to my radio show, you know that I’ve long felt that Herbert has been one of the most overrated entities in the NFL. Despite never winning anything of substance, including a single playoff game, so called “experts” have insisted on placing Herbert among the top half dozen or so quarterbacks in the NFL. With Mike McDaniel hired as the OC in Los Angeles, this was supposed to be the season where Herbert’s game actually elevated to the level people have insisted he’s played at since arriving in 2020. Instead, Herbert has been arguably the worst quarterback in the league, throwing ten picks in seven games, and being the steward of an offense that hasn’t scored a touchdown in 27 straight possessions. I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t enjoying Herbert’s meltdown validating my opinion of him as a player. I’d also be lying if I said I wasn’t terrified that his breakout game is going to happen this weekend against the beleaguered Texans defense. 1. C.J. Stroud’s run to (contractual) glory, continued Thankfully, the Texans clearly have the better quarterback in this matchup, and likely in every matchup in the schedule the remainder of the season. Despite the team’s 2-5 record, Stroud has been outstanding this season, as he is among the league leaders in passing yards, and has thrown 11 touchdowns to just one interception. The Chargers are 0-7, but their defense has been their strong suit this season. If the Texans are going to make a run at a playoff spot in the second half of the season, unless the defense recaptures its magic of 2025, they will likely need Stroud to keep playing at an elite level, and if he plays at that level for another ten games, he is going to get paid a LOT of money this offseason. away.blurb: Not just their versatile nickel, Jalen Pitre, but also starting strong safety Reed Blankenship as well, who's been deemed out since he went down with a concussion during the second quarter of Houston's Week 6 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. We'll know more about Blankenship's status now and moving forward once the Texans are back practicing on Wednesday, and we get an injury report designating the veteran safety as a full, limited, or non-participant. A concussion absence typically lasts around one to three weeks for most players around the league, but with Blankenship's newly discovered hand surgery, there's a chance that it takes more time for him to return as a starter on the back end of the Texans' defense. Alexander also notes that Blankenship is still in concussion protocol heading into the week against the Chargers, and will be a name to monitor as the week progresses. Texans safety Reed Blankenship, who remains in concussion protocol, also had surgery on his left hand not long after the Jaguars game, per a source. The Texans will see how he progress through the week. The team finds themselves at 2-5 following Week 8 of the season. That has them in second place in the AFC South and three games behind the Jacksonville Jaguars. In a reversal from last season, it is the team's defense that is holding them back. They are allowing 24.3 points per game (18th in NFL). That is a large change from 2025, when they allowed only 17.4 a game (2nd in NFL). Houston Texans running back David Montgomery (32) Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Outside of a three-touchdown performance in Week 1, Montgomery has been largely ineffective. Across five games this season, he has taken the ball 52 times for only 138 yards, resulting in a poor 2.7 yards per carry. During Week 5, the free agent acquisition pulled his groin in a game at the Tennessee Titans. He has been sidelined since. On Monday, the Texans signed RB Joshua Pitsenberger to the practice squad, per Jonathan M Alexander of the Houston Chronicle. Moments after this transaction was reported, Houston head coach Demeco Ryans said he did not have any significant update on Montgomery's health. His status for Week 9 appears to be in jeopardy. Pitsenberger is a 2026 undrafted free agent whom the Texans signed briefly after the draft. He has yet to appear in an NFL game but now becomes the fifth running back on the team, active roster and practice squad included. Houston has three RBs on the active roster, that being Woody Marks, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale. The offense this season has largely relied on the arm of quarterback C.J. Stroud.
