LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons . This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears. Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work. Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens (TNF) Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home. Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13 Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (Madrid) Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23 Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow. … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20 Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500. … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17 Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense. … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters. This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20 Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road. … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (-3) Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game, which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five. … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24 Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield. … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears (-6) (SNF) Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly chose Chicago to cover in Seattle last week, and I became even more confident in that pick when the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks' addition of Quenton Nelson is a great one, but I think the addition of Simmons is even better. He's the best defensive tackle in the NFL and makes life incredibly difficult for quarterbacks. In his first game for his new team, he recorded six tackles, one sack and two tackles for loss. Chicago's defense allowed just 3.0 yards per play with him

Yours truly correctly predicted the Chicago Bears to take down the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football. We move on to Week 9 and we're hoping for more upsets during this weekend's action. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 9 Upset Pick Minnesota Vikings (+150) vs. Buffalo Bills Josh Allen has a history of struggling against defenses as aggressive as the one Brian Flores operates. Allen did finally get by the Texans in Week 1, but that defense has drastically regressed this season. The Vikings’ defense has formed into what many expected to see out of the Texans in 2026. Minnesota is No. 1 in points allowed (13.3) and No. 2 in total defense (271.6). Yes, I do worry about Minnesota’s poor offense, but maybe Kyler Murray turns it around against the Bills’ poor defense, which is allowing 25.9 points per game. This will come down to Allen against the Vikings’ vaunted defense. Peter Dewey Week 9 Upset Pick Green Bay Packers (+140) vs. New England Patriots The Green Bay Packers can’t run the ball this season, averaging just 2.9 yards per carry, but that may not matter on the road against the New England Patriots in Week 9. New England is 20th in the league in EPA/Pass and eighth in EPA/Rush on defense, so the Packers and Jordan Love are likely going to lean on their elite passing game on Sunday. The Pack are coming off a mini-bye after playing on Thursday against Carolina, and they’ve won four of their last five games after a 1-2 start. Meanwhile, New England is extremely banged up at receiver and was in a dogfight against the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 8 before pulling away in the second half. The Pats have struggled a bit against elite competition this season, losing to Seattle, Jacksonville, and Chicago. Will we see a similar result against Green Bay? The Packers are quietly fifth in the NFL in EPA/Play on defense, and Love has been playing at a high level all season long. There aren’t a ton of great upset spots this week, but Green Bay’s recent form is intriguing against a banged-up New England squad. Iain MacMillan Week 9 Upset Pick Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+240) vs. Chicago Bears You can win a lot of games in the National Football League if you can run the ball effectively and play elite defense, and that's exactly what the Buccaneers have been doing. In fact, they shut the Falcons out last week without completing a single pass. They now enter this week ranked inside the top seven in every rushing metric, second in opponent EPA per play, and third in opponent success rate. We don't currently know what sort of form Baker Mayfield is in, but if he's in peak form when the Bucs need him to take to the air, Tampa Bay is going to be an extremely dangerous team. I have little bad to say about the Bears, who have proven me wrong about my preseason evaluation of them. The two teams have last met in 2022, a game won by the Packers at Lambeau Field. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , it very well could be the Patriots' turn to win now. Odds for Patriots vs. Packers in NFL Week 9 Spread: Patriots -2.5 Moneyline: Patriots -142 | Packers +120 Over/under: 47.5 Both the Patriots and Packers are entering Week 9 with identical 5-3 records. picks.headline: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9
picks.blurb: Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Experts Don't Like Patriots Chance to Defeat Packers in Week 9 (Rich Storry-Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots were able to take down the Miami Dolphins last week, improving their record to 5-3 on the season. New England didn't play the prettiest game on the field, but at this point for them, a win is a win. With all the injuries that the Patriots have seen take place, especially to the offense, the team has been able to stay alive. This week, the Patriots will be hosting the Green Bay Packers, giving the team a real challenge on its hands. Green Bay, like New England, has started to play much better of late, finally put things together on the field. The Packers will be entering the game with a record of 5-3, with both sides of the ball clicking for the team. New England is going to have to be careful in this game; otherwise, they could be on the losing end of the contest. Analysts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report all made picks for the game between the two teams. But six of the seven experts went with Green Bay to take down the Patriots in this matchup. Only Gagnon went with New England to win the game, despite this contest being played at home for the Patriots. But the Packers recent play likely has to do with how confident those around the league are heading into the week. One key for New England this week will be how quarterback Drake Maye performs, especially when it comes to turnovers. The Green Bay defense can be feisty at times, using its opportunistic nature to get the best of opposing quarterbacks. Maye will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that the Patriots have seen this year, going against this tough defense. But the veteran quarterback has done well this year , even with his issues earlier in the season. Against Green Bay, the Patriots may need to rely on the running game a little more, taking some pressure off Maye's shoulders. Head coach Mike Vrabel will have to put his signal-caller into a strong position to win, avoiding any issues. The offensive line will also need to hold up in the game, giving Maye time to throw the ball against this defensive front. Kickoff for the Patriots game against the Packers is scheduled to take place at 1:25 p.m. PT/4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough.

picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:27 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers have opened up as 2.5-point road underdogs on FanDuel against the New England Patriots in Week 9, coming off a mini-bye after beating the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football . The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he's posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots' chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic's playoff simulator . Green Bay's path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. According to The Athletic, the Packers have a 61 percent chance to make the playoffs if they beat the Patriots, but just a 39 percent chance if they lose. If Green Bay can split their trip to New England and their Week 10 game against the Minnesota Vikings, who are sitting in the driver's seat in the NFC North at the moment, they have about a 50-50 chance of making the playoffs going into their Week 11 bye week. After that, they should be getting some players back from injury lists, notably edge rusher Micah Parsons. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! Added to the distractions are all of the Rob Gronkowski highlight videos circulating, plus clips revisiting the 10-year anniversary of the 2016 Championship season. Click on even one of those and time vanishes down those very pleasant rabbit holes. Tom Brady returns to call his first game for FOX at Gillette Stadium. away.blurb: Nixon did not practice on Thursday while dealing with a groin injury. He was listed as limited on Wednesday. The veteran has not missed a game since signing with the Packers before the 2022 season, but he might need to practice Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the New England Patriots. Lloyd, who suffered through two injury-plagued seasons to start his NFL career, has his first injury of 2026: a knee injury. He was limited on Thursday. It's possible the Packers could return Chris Brooks this week, providing depth at running back if Lloyd can't go. Micah Parsons practiced in a limited capacity for the second straight day after returning on Wednesday. The Packers were in pads on Thursday. Parsons is not expected to play until Week 12 at the earliest. In addition to Nixon, the Packers did not have Zaire Franklin, Sean Rhyan, Travis Glover or Josh Whyle at Thursday's practice. All five are in danger of not playing against the Patriots. The Patriots made three changes: defensive lineman Christian Barmore practiced after missing Wednesday with an illness, while the team added cornerback Marcus Jones (foot) and safety Brenden Schooler (hamstring) to the injury report with new injuries. Receiver A.J. Brown didn't practice for the second straight day, so it's possible the Packers will be down a starting corner while the Patriots will be down two starting receivers (including former Packer Romeo Doubs, who is on injured reserve). The Packers and Patriots will have final practices on Friday before issuing status designations on the final injury report. home.headline: Patriots face $5 million salary cap dilemma ahead of NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: New England has limited financial flexibility, several roster needs and a chance to strengthen its playoff push. But Mike Vrabel and the Patriots must decide whether another major investment is worth the cost. New England enters the final days before the November 10 deadline with a 5-3 record, a legitimate chance to return to the playoffs and approximately $5 million in available salary cap space. New England entered the previous week with less than $2 million in available cap space before restructuring Henry’s contract. The move created enough breathing room to manage the roster and potentially absorb a modest contract before the trade deadline. That leaves Maye with a limited group of established receiving options. The Patriots have reportedly been monitoring the receiver market, although acquiring another prominent player at the position would create questions about roster construction once Brown and the other injured receivers return. For a team with limited cap space and several injured players expected to return, that may be the most practical strategy. Those developments give New England reason to believe its existing roster can remain competitive as injured players return. The Patriots have enough financial flexibility to pursue modest upgrades, and they have mechanisms available to create substantially more room if a compelling opportunity emerges. The New England Patriots have an opportunity to improve their roster before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The bigger question is how much they’re willing to sacrifice to make it happen. That last number could determine how aggressively the Patriots pursue reinforcements. According to Ben Volin of The Boston Globe , New England had approximately $5.35 million in cap space as of Tuesday, despite recently restructuring tight end Hunter Henry’s contract to create additional flexibility. The Patriots could free up considerably more money through additional contract restructures. However, they have shown little urgency to do so, potentially signaling that head coach Mike Vrabel and the front office are more interested in making targeted additions than completing another blockbuster trade. That approach would make sense for a franchise that has already invested heavily in its roster. With injuries mounting and the Patriots trying to establish themselves as legitimate AFC contenders, standing pat could leave New England vulnerable during the most important stretch of the season. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Darien Porter is questionable to return with a groin injury after going down without contact on the opening snap in the game against the New York Jets Sunday. Rookie Jermod McCoy took over for him at outside corner . The team then listed Porter as questionable with a groin injury . Raiders' Maxx Crosby Has Candid Words for Bay Area Return Darien Porter Injury: Why Did Raiders CB Leave Jets Game on Opening Play? Unlock the latest Heavy on Raiders news — direct to your inbox. The injury came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets in Week 8, and it leaves the Raiders watching the sideline to see whether a key cornerback can come back. Jets quarterback Geno Smith hit wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a long completion to start the game, with accounts of the gain ranging from 31 to 41 yards. Porter hit the turf without being touched , according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . Trainers helped Porter to the medical tent on the Raiders' sideline with the score still 0-0. He later emerged and was trying to regain his mobility under trainers' watchful eyes, according to Raiders beat writer Sam Warren. Why Isn’t Fernando Mendoza Playing for the Raiders Today? Insider Gives Timeline Las Vegas Raiders' Darien Porter Career Background Porter, 25, was born Jan. 6, 2001, in Bettendorf, Iowa, and is listed at 6 feet 2 inches and 195 pounds . He played receiver and cornerback at Bettendorf High School, catching 27 passes for 440 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior, and won a Class 4A state title in the 400 meters. He spent time at Iowa State from 2019 through 2024 , starting at receiver before moving to defensive back. Special teams made up most of his early role. He became a full-time starter in 2024, finishing with 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions and two passes defended, and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. Porter ran an unofficial 4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Raiders selected Porter in the third round of the 2025 draft, 68th overall. As a rookie, he played all 17 games, starting 10 , and totaled 42 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery. His rookie contract runs through 2028 . This season, Porter missed Week 2 against the Chargers because of a foot injury against the Dolphins in the opener. That was a separate issue from Sunday's injury. Before it, he had been targeted five times in that opener and allowed one catch for 12 yards , according to Pro Football Focus . Spread: Seahawks -10.5 (-113), Cardinals +10.5 (-107) Moneyline: Seahawks -650, Cardinals +475 Total: Over 42.5 (-105), Under 42.5 (-115) The -650 moneyline implies roughly 86.7% for Seattle to win outright. Put the spread and total together and the projected final comes out around Seahawks 26.5, Cardinals 16. Jaxon Smith-Njigba to score the first touchdown (+350) Bet365 has Smith-Njigba at +350 to open the scoring , an implied probability of roughly 22.2%. His -155 anytime price implies roughly 60.8%, and nobody else on the board is better than even money. The next shortest first-TD price is Zach Charbonnet at +650 (roughly 13.3%), a gap of about nine points. On the anytime market the gap is wider: Tyler Allgeier is next at +125, roughly 44.4%, about 16 points behind. A wide receiver at the top of a first-TD board is unusual. Running backs usually hold that spot because they get the carries near the goal line. Smith-Njigba has earned the exception. He was the focal point of a Super Bowl-winning offense last season, and the low total helps his case. At 42.5 points the market expects only five or six touchdowns, so the opening score carries more weight than usual. When touchdowns are scarce, the offense’s most reliable option is the logical favorite to get the first one. The argument against him is Seattle’s backfield. Charbonnet (+650) and rookie Jadarian Price (+700) together come to roughly 25.8% to score first, more than Smith-Njigba on his own. That is a split workload, and the board is saying that when Seattle reaches the goal line it will often hand the ball off. The visible Seattle names (Smith-Njigba, Charbonnet, Price and AJ Barner) add up to roughly 57.5% before the sportsbook’s margin is removed, against roughly 23.0% for Arizona’s Allgeier and Trey McBride. The market is confident Seattle scores first. It is less sure which Seahawk does it. First and anytime touchdown scorer odds Jaxon Smith-Njigba Zach Charbonnet Tyler Allgeier Jadarian Price Allgeier is coming off a 147-yard rushing day against Dallas, and McBride remains Arizona’s top target. They are the only Cardinals on the visible board. Quarterback passing yards Bet365’s passing yardage ladders show how the market rates the two quarterbacks. Sam Darnold is -130 to reach 225 yards (roughly 56.5%) and +150 to reach 250. His last five games came in at 168, 195, 278, 257 and 188. Minshew is -110 for 200 yards (roughly 52.4%) and +165 for 225, priced off a single relief appearance. Same Game Parlays on the board Bet365’s featured Same Game Parlays for this game: TD Trio (+950, $10 pays $105): Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price each to score a TD Same Game Parlay (+1800, $10 pays $190): Smith-Njigba, Charbonnet, Tyler Allgeier and Trey McBride each to score a TD End Zone to End Zone Action (+3500, $10 pays $360): Both teams over 12.5 points in the first half and both teams over 12.5 points in the second half The TD Trio is a bet on a Seattle blowout, with all three of its top scoring options cashing. End Zone to End Zone Action needs each team to score at least 26 points, a combined 52 or more, nearly 10 points over the posted total. That explains the +3500 price. Cardinals vs. Seahawks prediction and best bet Seattle is the better team and should win this game. The question is whether it wins by 11 or more, and the numbers make that harder than the spread suggests. A 42.5 total and a 10.5-point spread don’t sit easily together. For Seattle to cover in a game with that little scoring, it needs a result like 27-16 or 24-13, with Arizona held to two scores or fewer. A single late Arizona touchdown changes everything. The Seahawks are also 3-5 against the spread this season and lost by 17 on Monday night. A defending champion at .500, laying double digits, has to be judged on how it is playing now, and right now it isn’t playing like a team that wins by margin. The case for Seattle is real. The Seahawks are 9-1 against the spread in their last 10 meetings with Arizona, per Sports Illustrated , and Minshew’s three-touchdown half came against a Dallas team, not on the road at Lumen Field. If Arizona’s offense stalls early, 10.5 can come quickly. Even so, the low total does most of the work here. Fewer points mean fewer chances for Seattle to build a margin, and the hook on 10.5 covers a 10-point loss, one of the more common final margins in the league. Best bet: Cardinals +10.5 (-107) at Bet365 For the prop, Smith-Njigba at +350 is the best value on a low-scoring board. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Winners, losers as Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy over debts from crash, alleged assault An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). There was hope for the Seattle Seahawks after a dominating win over the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7 as they prepared for another big game against the Chicago Bears. The Seahawks were set to utilize several key players in hopes of getting back to the top of the NFC standings. Among them were rookies who the Seahawks need to impact for the franchise’s stability. Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said. The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Bleacher Report • 2h Knicks Call Out Taylor Swift 😬 Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday. Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. 7 Backup QBs Starting in Week 9 Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week. Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1). A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . home.headline: Week 9 Injury Report: Cardinals at Seahawks
home.blurb: The Seahawks continued their week of preparation ahead of their Week 9 game against the Cardinals with a relatively long list of players not practicing. Given the short week coming off a Monday night game, it's entirely possible that some of the absences are precautionary, but it will be something to watch when the team puts out game statuses on Friday. Two players were new on the injury report, outside linebacker Derick Hall who did not practice due to a back injury, and linebacker Ernest Jones IV , who was limited with an ankle injury. Two players, outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and left guard link-placeholder-1 , went from limited Wednesday to not practicing on Thursday. Listed as non-participants for the second straight day were left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (quadricep/ribs), outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (foot), nose tackle Brandon Pili (back), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger). For the Cardinals, guard Jon Gaines (ankle), running back Bam Knight (concussion) and tackle Jayden Williams (knee) were non-participants for the second day in a row. Cornerback Max Melton (knee) was new to the injury report with a knee injury, one of three players who were limited due to injury along with guard Isaiah Adams (ankle) and defensive tackle Walter Nolen (ankle). When Macdonald was asked about Williams on Wednesday, Macdonald said he, as well as Cross and Shaheed, "all have a chance to play. We haven't ruled anybody out yet." Among those listed as limited was quarterback Drew Lock , who is expected to start in Darnold's place. Lock has been dealing with an elbow injury that also had him limited the last two weeks and led to him serving as the emergency third quarterback behind Darnold and Jalen Milroe the past two games, as opposed to his usual role as the No. 2 quarterback. Also limited were guard Anthony Bradford (knee), running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle). For the Cardinals, guard Jon Gaines (ankle), running Bam Knight (concussion) and tackle Jayden Williams (knee) were non participants due to injury, while defensive tackle Walter Nolen (ankle) and guard Isaiah Adams (ankle) were limited. Baker Mayfield and the Bucs won in Week 8 without completing a pass, and after an 0-4 start they’ve won three of their last four games to put themselves right back in the mix to win a terrible NFC South. The Bucs have back-to-back division wins over Carolina and Atlanta, but things will be a lot tougher on the road against the Bears and an MVP candidate in Williams . Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Oddsmakers have set Chicago as a six-point favorite at home as it looks to get to 7-2 before a Week 10 bye. The Bears are still behind the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings – who beat them earlier this season – in the NFC North standings. Let’s take a look at the opening odds for this primetime matchup in a loaded Week 9. Buccaneers vs. Bears Odds, Spread and Total for NFL Week 9 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bucs +6 (-112) Bears -6 (-108) 46.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been any real movement in the odds for this game since they opened on Sunday night, even with the Bears picking up an upset win over Seattle. This is a battle between two very different teams, as Tampa Bay has relied heavily on the running game and its defense to get back in the playoff mix while the Bears are one of the best offenses in football. Chicago ranks 10th in EPA/Play, 11th in success rate and tied for 13th in yards per play this season despite the fact that Williams has missed three full games and part of the team’s Week 2 loss to Minnesota. When the former No. 1 overall pick has been on the field, Ben Johnson’s club has been humming on the offensive end, dropping 34 points in Week 8 against a Seattle defense that is No. 1 in the NFL in success rate and entered Week 8 at No. 1 in yards per play allowed. Tampa Bay’s defense is now No. 1 in EPA/Play after picking off Michael Penix Jr. several times in a rain-soaked matchup in Week 8, but things won’t be nearly as easy against Williams. On the bright side for the Bucs, they should be able to run the ball (eighth in EPA/Rush this season) against a Bears defense that is allowing 4.4 yards per carry in 2026. Chicago traded for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of Week 8, but the Tampa Bay running game – led by Bucky Irving – won’t be easy to stop on Sunday night. I lean with the Bears to win this game, and it’ll be interesting to see if the odds move at all with both teams trending in the right direction with the halfway point of the 2026 season upon us. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Jaguars (-10) over Ravens Even at -10, the line seems too low. The Jaguars have three wins by 24 points or more and two came against the 5-3 Browns and the 5-3 Patriots. They're good. There could be a letdown facing Baltimore undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano, and it's possible the Ravens rally around Fagnano for a season-saving performance with Jacoby Brissett on the way next week. But this seems like a huge ask for the Ravens, who have scored 13 or fewer points in three straight games. Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. Last week : 7-7 Season to date: 53-65-2

(Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sam Householder · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to cap off a hat trick of primetime games. They're hoping to finish the three-game stretch at 3-0 as they head into their bye week, but a tough Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad stands in the way. Chicago is riding high after back-to-back wins over last season's Super Bowl participants, but the Bucs should not be overlooked. Will the Bears fall victim to a trap spot or will Ben Johnson continue to keep the team focused and not let them buy into the hype the media has built up around them? For Tampa Bay, it's a chance to shake off their 0-4 start and prove their improvements over the last month weren't a fluke. The Bucs come in having won three of their last four games and the only loss came in overtime. Their defense ranks first in the league. However, the offense has been clunky. Over the last two weeks, they've won resoundingly with virtually no passing game (in last week's 16-0 win, no "virtually" modifier was needed). Dive into the Bucs and what it will take for the Bears to remain on a winning streak. Tampa Bay Buccaneers SB Nation site: Bucs Nation Record: 3-5, second in the NFC South Last week: 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons Game day, time, TV: Sunday, 7:20 p.m. CT, NBC Sunday Night Football Spread: Bears -6.5 Bears all-time record against: 40-22 Historical meetings: Week 10 of the 2001 season. The Bears defense held the Bucs' offense in check in the first half, allowing only three Tampa field goals. Jim Miller and Marty Booker had their connection going though. They connected for three touchdowns –28-, 44- and 66-yards. A late comeback by the Bucs gave the Bears a scare. Brad Johnson rushed for a 1-yard score and hit Mike Alstott for a 2-point conversion with 2:29 left in the game. Chicago ended up punting back to Tampa but Johnson was picked off by Tony Parrish. Anthony Thomas fumbled, giving the Bucs new life. Johnson hit Warrick Dunn along the sideline but R.W. McQuarters was flagged for unnecessary roughness, giving them another 15 yards. That allowed Tampa to attempt a 48-yard field goal, but they missed it as time expired. The Bears won 27-24. Last meeting: Week 2 of 2023. The Bears offense had its moments, but the defense was shredded. Mike Evans had 171 yards and a touchdown, while Baker Mayfield threw for 317 yards. Justin Fields threw for 211 yards and rushed for a TD. However, he threw two interceptions. DJ Moore had 104 receiving yards. Chase Claypool also had a touchdown. A late pick-six by Shaquil Barrett off Fields sealed a 27-17 Bucs win. Injury report: The Bucs listed five players on their injury report. Limited participation RB Kenny Gainwell (hip) S Tykee Smith (ankle) Did not participate OLB Yaya Diably (knee) WR Emeka Egbuka (foot) DL Elijah Roberts (personal) Offense: The Buccaneers come into Chicago ranked 20th in points and 25th in yards. Their passing offense ranks 29th, while their rushing offense ranks first. Quite the disparity, but the numbers are backed by the past two weeks when they've passed for a total of 62 yards. Baker Mayfield (61.8 pct cmp./679 yds./3 TD/2 INT) missed three games with a thumb injury that he's now playing through. However, he has done minimal passing since returning and Tampa's numbers reflect that. Emeka Egbuka (28 rec./240 yds./2 TD) is the leading receiver for the Bucs, but he's been injured. Chris Godwin (27/243/0), Cade Otton (19/186/0) and the running backs Bucky Irbing (18/78/1) and Kenneth Gainwell (12/61/1) are the other receiving leaders for Tampa. Tez Johnson (9/178/1) and Ted Hurst (11/168/1) have also caught some passes. On the ground, however, Irving (148 att./728 yds./5 TD) and Gainwell (58/289/0) are getting the production for the Bucs. They're each averaging 5.0 yards per carry. In fact, every Tampa player with a rushing attempt is averaging at least 5 yards per carry. Defense: Tampa's defense comes in ranked fifth in points and third in yards allowed. They rank eighth in passing defense and second in rushing defense. The dominant unit is led by LBs Josiah Trotter (68 tkls/1 INT/3 PD/1 sk/3 TFL/1 QB hits) and Alex Anzalone (42 tkls/3 INT/1 sk/2 TFL/1 QB hits/3 PD). S Tykee Smith (1 INT/43 tkls/3 TFL/4 QB hits/2 PD) is also making plays all over. Up front, OLBs David Walker (4 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits), YaYa Diaby (3 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits/2 PD/1 INT) and Al-Quadin Muhammad (2 sk/1 FF/1 PD/4 QB hits/2 TFL) are getting after opposing QBs. Veteran A'Shawn Robinson (1 sk/2 INT/3 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits) is playing well. In the secondary, Jacob Parrish (2 INT/13 PD/3 TFL) leads the league in pass breakups. Zyon McCollum (30 tkls/2 INT/9 PD/1 TFL) and Keionte Scott (39 tkls/4 PD/1 sk/1 QB hit) are making plays, too. Key matchups: It's a classic battle of the trenches. The Bears OL needs to best Tampa's DL to establish the run and allow Caleb Williams to use play action to take downfield shots. Keeping Williams clean will allow the offense to be at its best. On defense, the Bears need to slow Irving and Gainwell down and not allow them to chew up the clock and get easy yards. Forcing Baker into passing situations and play from behind benefits the Bears. The Bucs have allowed more than 300 yards of offense only three times this year. They beat the Cowboys 24-16 but lost to the Cincinnati Bengals (33-27) and Pittsburgh Steelers (26-19 in OT). The Bears have had less than 300 yards of offense in their two losses. Baker Mayfield has 14 pass attempts and 64 passing yards in the past two games. He's completed only half of his attempts. The Bucs defense is tied for the best DADOT at 6.6. Their pressure percentage is fifth-worst at 19.3 percent, despite having the seventh-highest blitz percentage at 33.6 percent. Tampa's pass defense is really good. Opposing QBs have a 74.9 rating against them and just 205.9 yards per game. Can the Bears finish off their trifecta of primetime games against top defenses undefeated? Is this a trap spot for Chicago?

away.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson Jr. ruled out vs. Buccaneers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Several key defenders are questionable for Sunday's game. FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Running back Brian Robinson Jr. has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, meaning it will be the second straight game he misses due to a hamstring injury. Robinson is the only player ruled out, but many are listed as questionable, including several key defenders. Compare that to 7.6 targets and 52 yards per game in three full games with Murray. Wentz will need to feed his star wideout if the Vikings want to end the night with a statement win. 2. Vikings' defense holds the Bills to less than 300 total yards This one is a swing, but I’m betting on the Vikings defense to defend their home turf against one of the best offensive units in the NFL. Josh Allen and the Bills are averaging 393.1 total yards per game, trailing only the Lions. The Vikings defense, meanwhile, allows the second-fewest yards per game at only 271.6. Getting to Allen early while preventing him from taking off will be the key. This will be one of their hardest challenges of the year, but I'm certain defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit are preparing hard for this one. The Vikings need DC Brian Flores to give his best performance of the season so far when they face the Bills on Monday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota’s defense put up a strong effort in Detroit last week, but a total lack of help from the offense eventually opened the door for Jahmyr Gibbs to ice the game. Carson Wentz throws for Vikings’ season-high in yardage The ingredients for a Wentz legacy performance are starting to add up. The Vikings’ passing game needs a serious boost;o Jefferson and Jordan Addison need targets, and head coach Kevin O’Connell almost certainly wants to silence the doubts around his offensive scheme. Time to let it rip. The Carson Wentz career arc is like no other. pic.twitter.com/wFV21ULa0W The Bills’ 254.7 passing yards allowed per game are the third-highest total in the NFL this season, an average higher than any passing performance we’ve seen this year from a Vikings passer. Murray’s 247 yards against the Dolphins is currently the season high, but I think that changes Monday. Mark me down for Wentz over 250 through the air. Earlier this week, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and that he'd be re-evaluated this week. Murray and the Vikings don't play until Monday night in Week 9, so they have yet to release a practice report since their first official session will come on Thursday. That has left the quarterback's status in limbo with the Vikings (6-1) looking to remain in the top spot in the NFC North. NFL insider Ian Rapoport doesn't believe that Murray is dealing with a long-term injury, but he did mention that Murray may not play since he's a mobile quarterback and can't move around as well. That would pave the way for veteran Carson Wentz to get the start, something he did in place of Murray in Week 2. Sports Illustrated spoke to oddsmakers about the injury a,d BetMGM's Christian Cipollini, a Senior Trading Manager, explained that the spread would move quite a bit if Wentz gets the start. "You'll see this line go back down to Bills -3 if Kyler is healthy and does play," Cipollini said. "If it is Wentz this line will probably close around Bills -6. Wouldn't impact futures at the moment, the strength of this team is built through the defense and coaching so a rare one where QB play is more of a bonus for this team." DraftKings Sportbsook had moved the Vikings to 2.5-point underdogs at home in this matchup, but the line has since shifted back up to Minnesota +3.5. The Vikings opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night , but they were gaining ground at home before the Murray update was released. There's no doubt that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as an upgrade over Wentz. For now, bettors and fans have to wait and see if Murray is able to log at least a limited session in Thursday's practice. Based on the latest odds movement, he seems to be 50/50 for Monday's showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills. This season, Murray has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five scores and three picks while adding 29 carries for 167 yards on the ground. The Vikings are in the bottom three in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on offense, so Wentz doesn't have a high bar to clear if he's the quarterback on Monday night. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.headline: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills
picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Rams’ Myles Garrett reportedly on track to be activated in Week 9 TRENDING Ravens look ugly on 'TNF' LSU women break D-I record Week 9 fantasy sleepers NFL trade deadline buzz Ranking NBA rookie phenoms Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue.
