home.headline: Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury and Struggles
home.blurb: Wentz's numbers from his limited playing time earlier this season whilst Murray was in concussion protocol far exceed what the former first overall pick has managed to accomplish since taking back the reins. Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury and Struggles Unlock the latest Heavy on Vikings news — direct to your inbox. The Minnesota Vikings have been accused of preparing a "soft benching" for struggling quarterback Kyler Murray for much of this past week as the former Arizona Cardinal deals with a hamstring injury. Having yet to announce an injury report, considering that they play on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills , head coach Kevin O'Connell had not given much concreted indication as to what Murray's practice or playing status might look like over the coming days. However, speaking to the media on Thursday, O'Connell revealed that Murray's injury will force him to miss Monday's game, and that Carson Wentz will start instead. " The #Vikings are planning to start Carson Wentz on MNF against the #Bills , as Kyler Murray's hamstring injury would limit his mobility. Murray also could make it worse by playing." Ian Rapoport reported on Thursday. Is This a Soft Benching for Kyler Murray? The Super Bowl champion from 2018 has a passer rating 20 points higher than Murray, averages 0.44 more yards per throw, and has a far better touchdown to interception ratio (3:0 v.s. 5:3). Minnesota have a gruelling three-game schedule against the Bills, Packers and 49ers over the next three weeks, and whilst the injury may simply be a coincidence, it could also be that O'Connell knows he will need his best at the helm in order to remain contenders to top the NFC North and the conference as a whole. home.headline: Vikings trade for QB on the table, new NFL rumors reveal amid Kyler Murray injury
home.blurb: Palmer noted that the Vikings "know the market" and which quarterbacks are available, as general manager Nolan Teasley has been working the phones and looking into trades to address multiple positions. If there is an available quarterback who can help improve the NFL's No. 27 scoring offense, then it is worth exploring, but there may not be an obvious upgrade out there unless the Las Vegas Raiders unexpectedly decide to part with Kirk Cousins despite a 4-4 record and playoff contention. The idea of trading for a quarterback is reportedly "on the table" for the Minnesota Vikings ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. During an appearance on the Thursday Night Football postgame show, Prime Video NFL insider James Palmer reported on what he has heard about the Vikings and their potential pursuit of a quarterback: While the Vikings reportedly "still believe" in starting quarterback Kyler Murray, Palmer added that the team's performance on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills this coming week could determine whether Minnesota makes a move at QB. Murray will not start on Monday night due to a hamstring injury that has him listed as week-to-week , meaning backup Carson Wentz will be under center. Signed as a free agent this past offseason after getting released by the Arizona Cardinals, Murray has gone 5-1 in six starts, but his production has been modest, completing 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions, while also rushing for 167 yards. Murray suffered a concussion early in the Vikings' first game of the season, prompting Wentz to replace him. Wentz led Minnesota to a win in that game and then started and won the next game before Murray returned to the lineup. Over the two games Wentz appeared in, he completed 59.0 percent of his passing attempts for 276 yards with three touchdowns and no picks. Both Murray and Wentz are viable options for the Vikings moving forward this season, but the organization potentially wanting to take an aggressive approach is understandable. Minnesota is tied for the best record in the NFL at 6-1, and it has the No. 1 defense in the league in terms of points allowed at 13.3 per game. The Vikings also have a superstar wide receiver in Justin Jefferson who has not been used to the best of his ability.
